Zelensky Says Putin ‘Needs Trump,’ May Offer De-Escalation Before Winter
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:38:11 UTC
05:38:11 KST

President Volodymyr Zelensky said that he believes Russian President Vladimir Putin “needs” US President Donald Trump and is unlikely to “antagonize” him ahead of winter – even as Moscow views the season as a chance to weaken Ukraine.
Zelensky made the remarks in an interview with Axios on Monday, Sept. 7, while also revealing possible new outcomes of the negotiations, following the weekend discussions in Kyiv with senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Although he declined to disclose further details, Zelensky said that “there are ideas around energy [facilities] and around grain [shipments], around electricity [facilities] and around oil and gas [exports].”
“We have different interests, Russia and we,” he continued.
Asked whether Putin might want to give Trump a diplomatic win ahead of the US elections, Zelensky confirmed, saying he believes that Putin might be pressured by the Trump administration to de-escalate the war.
Kremlin relies on winter pressure
Zelensky noted that he remains convinced Putin views the approaching winter as leverage to push Kyiv into further concessions.
“Russia really thinks that this winter can help them to break us,” he told Axios, suggesting Moscow anticipates a renewed assault on infrastructure may leave Ukraine “more compromising.”
He maintained that Kyiv has already exhausted its capacity for concessions and that any settlement would require firm security guarantees alongside economic backing.
Burnham, Trump Agree to Keep Working Toward Ukraine-Russia Ceasefire
Meanwhile, Putin continues to insist on his own terms for peace, holding firm to demands that Ukraine cede the remainder of Donetsk and Luhansk regions before any frontline compromise can be reached, citing Moscow’s battlefield victories – the same victories that have been debunked by independent analysts.
Zelensky also pointed to Ukraine’s capacity to hit Russia back. “When they attacked our electricity, we blocked their possibility to sell oil and gas,” he said.
Envoys say Russia willing to talk
The US delegation visiting Kyiv reportedly conveyed to Zelensky that Moscow is prepared to engage in negotiations, even as Russia increases its aggression against Ukraine, casting heavy doubt on that possibility.
Regardless, the meetings appear to have moved forward, as demonstrated by all three sides on Monday; Witkoff confirmed “substantive progress” had been made, “including movement on scheduling additional trilateral talks;” Zelensky echoed the development by saying that Ukraine was planning its “next steps” following three rounds of negotiations in Kyiv; and – though offering no timeline for the meetings – the Kremlin said that Moscow did not rule out resuming the trilateral format.
Strategy ahead of winter
Zelensky told Axios that Washington’s current strategy combines two goals – reopening formal talks and securing informal arrangements to prevent an escalation during the winter season.
He described this reading of the situation as “very close to the reality of these conversations,” adding that the goal would be to find steps – before or during the winter – “which can bring [the] sides closer to the peace.”
According to Zelensky, the US is also assembling a separate winter aid package for Ukraine. “It’s not only about missiles,” he said. “It’s also about LNG [liquefied natural gas]... and it’s also about steps of de-escalation.”
Washington has noticeably changed its stance towards Ukraine over past year. Until 2025, it remained Moscow-aligned, with Trump refusing to call Russia the aggressor and blaming Ukraine for starting the war.
Citing Ukraine’s battlefield success, Trump has since gone as far as calling Russia the likely loser in its own war, while simultaneously floating the idea of granting Ukraine the license to domestically produce its own Patriots during Zelensky’s visit to the White House on July 28.
Around the same time, the envoys agreed to visit Kyiv. Their weekend trip marked the first time they had visited Ukraine since becoming presidential intermediaries.
Meanwhile, they had maintained extensive contact with Moscow.
Kyiv intends to use the diplomatic momentum
Zelensky said Kyiv intends to use the upcoming months – particularly September and October – to revive diplomatic momentum, floating the United Nations (UN) General Assembly session in New York as a potential setting for further discussions with US officials.
“Without dialogue… we will not have a result,” Zelensky said, expressing optimism that Trump could help launch genuine negotiations ahead of winter.
He argued that Kyiv is currently in a better position on the battlefield than it previously was – even as Russian drone and missile attacks continue, and as Ukraine faces shortages in its air defense.
Zelensky also urged additional US sanctions on Russia, describing them as a key source of leverage. “Putin needs money,” he said. “Putin wants money to continue the war.”

triangular timber structure encloses tsukumo kiln ceramic studio in kobe, japan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:35:58 UTC
05:35:58 KST

Rotated Timber Frames Define the Studio’s Triangular Structure
Set on a hill within the rural landscape of Kobe, Japan, Tsukumo Kiln by Dept. + OAAA is a ceramic studio surrounded by fields and mountains. Conceived as a working space for ceramic production, the 80.32-sqm building responds to its open setting through a triangular plan, a column-free central workspace, and a continuous translucent envelope.
The structure is organized around three timber portal frames, each rotated 60 degrees from the next. This arrangement produces an equilateral triangular geometry in plan and establishes a building without a conventional front, back, or dominant direction. The same geometric operation defines both the structural organization and the spatial character of the studio.
To maintain an open interior suitable for ceramic production, steel tension rods are incorporated into the structural system to pull and lift the timber beams. This reduces the need for interior columns and leaves the central working area largely unobstructed. The exposed relationship between the timber frames and steel tension members makes the structural forces visible within the workspace.
Translucent FRP skin wraps the Studio in a Continuous Envelope
The collaborative design team between studios Dept. + OAAA encloses the exterior in folded FRP panels whose profile follows the geometry of the roof. The roof and walls are therefore treated as a continuous envelope rather than separate architectural elements. The FRP panels were joined on site to create a visually seamless exterior surface. Their translucent quality responds to changing daylight, giving the building different appearances according to weather, time of day, and viewing direction.
Construction was developed as part of the architectural process, with geometry, structural logic, material behavior, fabrication, and on-site assembly considered together. The timber framing, steel tension members, and site-assembled FRP skin retain their distinct material characteristics while operating as a unified architectural system.
Inside, the triangular organization creates multiple relationships with the surrounding landscape, while the column-free workspace allows flexibility in arranging kilns, worktables, storage, and production areas. The limited material palette and repeated geometric operation generate the building’s structure, enclosure, and spatial organization simultaneously, with its architectural form emerging from the interaction between construction, material, and ceramic production.

CASA 47: what the new national public housing portal offers and how it works
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:30:06 UTC
05:30:06 KST

The government unveils the first portal for national public housing, with income-linked rents and 14-year contracts. Sánchez defends state intervention to boost supply and secure access to housing.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez on Monday unveiled the first portal (source in Spanish) for the state public housing stock, launched by the State Housing and Land Agency CASA 47. The platform starts with 800 homes available and, according to La Moncloa, a further 1,500 spread across the country will be added "very soon".
During the closing session of the event "More public housing, more affordable housing", held in Madrid, Sánchez said the aim is to make it easier to access housing at affordable prices and lamented that "for far too many people, looking for a home has turned into an obstacle course".
What is the CASA 47 portal?
The portal will allow users to consult the available public housing stock and apply for a home according to each applicant's needs and financial capacity. According to Sánchez, quoted in a statement (source in Spanish), the procedure will be "swift and transparent" and will allow people to know at all times how the allocation process is progressing.
The initial offer will be expanded with new homes and flats becoming available every quarter, as part of the government's goal of increasing the state stock of affordable public housing.
What will the rents be?
Rent levels will take into account the characteristics of each home and the economic reality of each municipality and region. The government also stipulates that those who access these homes will not have to spend more than 30% of their income on rent.
Sánchez has described these rents as "affordable rent" and stressed the need to achieve "realistic rents for real wages". Contracts will have an initial term of 14 years, with the possibility of being extended up to 75 years, the prime minister explained.
Will the homes remain part of the public stock?
One of the key aspects highlighted by Sánchez is the permanent protection of CASA 47 homes. The prime minister has pledged that they will be protected "forever" and cannot be removed from the public stock when the economic or political cycle changes.
Sánchez criticised the fact that in recent decades protected housing has lost that status and insisted that "something like this must never happen again". In his view, "what is built through everyone's efforts must remain at the service of everyone".
Why does the government defend intervening in the market?
The prime minister explicitly defended public intervention in the housing market. "Some will say that this measure is 'interventionist' in the housing market. It is, and proudly so, because the market is broken," he said.
Sánchez also pointed out that the government has multiplied by eight the budget allocated to housing and highlighted the implementation of the Housing Law in designated high-pressure areas.
According to his figures, more than nine million people live in one of the 317 municipalities designated as high-pressure areas. He also cited Barcelona, where he says the price of new contracts has fallen by 4.7% since it was designated a high-pressure area, and several municipalities in Gipuzkoa, where prices are said to have dropped by almost 4%.
How many affordable homes does the government plan to mobilise?
The government places CASA 47 within a broader strategy to build and mobilise affordable housing. Sánchez recalled that more than 120,000 affordable rental homes have already been mobilised and that during the first quarter of this year 2,800 new homes were put out to tender, the largest volume of public tendering in 18 years, according to his figures.
The 2026–2030 State Housing Plan (source in Spanish), approved in April, has a budget of 7 billion euros, three times more than the previous plan.
What role will the authorities play?
The Minister for Housing and the Urban Agenda, Isabel Rodríguez, also quoted in the statement, argued that the allocation process must be public and said that the aim is to prevent a repeat of cases in which a social housing development is awarded to "councillors, municipal architects or relatives".
Rodríguez also highlighted the recovery of Sareb's assets to make available more than 42,000 homes and 2,500 plots of land, as well as the tendering of almost 2,500 homes currently being processed.
Finally, the minister urged regional governments and town councils to "pull together in the same direction" and said she was confident of also reaching agreements in parliament.

Albares thanks the 2,200 Spanish aid workers working for sustainable development around the world
Spain
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
22:29:00 CEST
05:29:00 KST

The Minister for Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation, José Manuel Albares, today opened the event commemorating Aid Workers' Day at the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID), under the slogan “Strategic partnerships for a zero-hunger world".
“Today we pay tribute to an essential and indispensable part of our foreign action: work that is particularly difficult in the current international context and more necessary than ever," the Minister said, thanking the 2,192 Spanish development cooperation professionals currently working in different countries and international organisations. “The Ministry is working every day to restore normality in Ceuta," Albares said in his remarks. “That is why this weekend we sent equipment from AECID's START team with capacity to accommodate more than 600 people."
Following the opening of the event to mark Aid Workers' Day, which is celebrated every 8 September, the Secretary of State for International Cooperation, Eva Granados, and the Director of AECID, Victoria Tur, spoke before a round-table discussion with prominent professionals from different areas of development cooperation. The event concluded with remarks by Teresa Godoy, President of the Association of Development Cooperation Professionals (APC), José Ángel Calle, AECID's Director of Partnerships, and Nacho Esteve, President of the Coordinator of Development Organisations. 
A COMMUNITY PRESENT AROUND THE WORLD 
Spanish aid workers carry out their work in all regions where Spanish Cooperation is present. Sub-Saharan Africa has the largest number, with 1,018 people, followed by Central America, with 355, and South America, with 352. Aid workers are also posted in Europe, Asia, the Maghreb and the Middle East.
This presence enables Spanish Cooperation to provide continuous support to its partner countries and to gain first-hand knowledge of the needs and priorities of the communities with which it works.
The aid worker community comprises 1,166 women and 1,026 men, a composition that also reflects the importance of women in the different professional areas of international cooperation. Of the aid workers, 409 are under the age of 35, while 1,776 are over that age, forming a professional community that combines experience and new generations.
PROFESSIONALS FROM DIFFERENT FIELDS 
Spanish Cooperation is also a shared endeavour involving professionals from different institutions and organisations.
Spanish aid workers include 651 people linked to non-governmental development organisations (NGDOs), 535 working in international organisations, 587 belonging to religious organisations and 201 AECID professionals, as well as others working in different fields.
This diversity is one of the strengths of Spanish Cooperation and makes it possible to bring together knowledge, capacities and experience to tackle challenges that no country can address alone.
PARTNERSHIPS AND ZERO HUNGER 
This year's celebration of Aid Workers' Day, which takes place on 7 September, is dedicated to food security and the fight against hunger, under the slogan “Strategic partnerships for a zero-hunger world". AECID brought together at its headquarters aid workers representing different areas of development cooperation to share experiences and reflect on the role of partnerships in guaranteeing the right to food.
The event also provided an opportunity to share progress in drafting Spanish Cooperation's new Food Security and Fight against Hunger Strategy, placing the right to food among the priorities of the cooperation agenda and highlighting the importance of combining capacities, knowledge and resources to address a challenge that particularly affects the most vulnerable populations.
WORKING AND BUILDING TOGETHER 
Aid Workers' Day is an opportunity to recognise the work of those carrying out their activities outside Spain and, at the same time, to recall that development cooperation is not merely about providing resources, but also about supporting processes, strengthening capacities and working alongside the institutions and communities of partner countries.
In an international context marked by humanitarian crises, conflicts, climate change and growing inequalities, the work of aid workers is particularly important in making the principles of global solidarity and sustainable development a reality.
Through Spanish Cooperation, AECID recognises and thanks all those who, in different places and professional fields, contribute every day to building a fairer, more sustainable and more supportive world.
* The Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) is the state agency responsible for promoting, programming, coordinating and executing the public policies of Spanish cooperation for sustainable development, humanitarian action and education for global citizenship.

Giuliani says Mamdani should skip 9/11 ceremony during rant against Islam

New York mayor Zohran Mamdani is set to come face-to-face with Rudy Giuliani at the main September 11 memorial service, just days after the former mayor – who led the city at the time of the 2001 terrorist attacks – disparaged his Muslim religion and said he should skip the ceremony.
In an interview with right-leaning Newsmax at the weekend, Giuliani said: “Having lost friends there and being very close to many of the families, it offends me that he’s coming.”
Mamdani confirmed on Monday, while attending a breakfast celebrating New York’s J’ouvert and West Indian Day Parade celebrations in Brooklyn, that he would attend the main ceremony and multiple 9/11 events on Friday, to stand with the families of those who died and first responders – as he did last year before taking office.
“I’m proud to be the mayor of this city. I love this city. I love this country,” he said. “What I want this week to be a focus on is on the families whose loved ones were stolen from them 25 years ago in the horrific act of terror of September 11, and a focus also on the first responders who did everything they could.”
The mayor and his office have declined to respond to Giuliani’s remarks.
Giuliani, the former mayor and a close ally of Donald Trump, has said he will also attend this year’s ceremony to mark the attacks by terrorists representing al-Qaida, who flew hijacked passenger planes into the twin towers of the World Trade Center in lower Manhattan on September 11 2001.
Reflecting pools with waterfalls constructed on the footprints of the towers and a 9/11 museum now mark the site that was dubbed Ground Zero in the aftermath of the attacks, and where each year the names of the almost 3,000 people who died are read out by survivors and loved ones, in a solemn ceremony attended by national and local leaders.
In the interview with Newsmax, Giuliani was asked if Mamdani should skip the ceremony. “Well, there’s no question he should,” he said.
Giuliani was mayor of New York City from 1994 to 2001. He ran unsuccessfully for president and, more recently, has been an attorney to and a staunch ally of Donald Trump.
In the convoluted tirade on air on Saturday, Giuliani threw insults and baseless comparisons. He appeared to draw parallels between Mamdani’s faith and the 9/11 hijackers acting on the extremist orders of Osama bin Laden, the jihadist militant and terrorist leader killed by US forces during the Obama administration.
He remarked that the terrorists brought their ideological opposition to the United States “in the name of the Muslim religion” and “weren’t hiding it like Mamdani is trying to hide it”. He also declared the opinion that the mayor supports a notion that Islam should be the dominant religion.
Mamdani has previously spoken about how an Islamophobic backlash built after the 2001 attacks and had made anti-Muslim prejudice “a fact of life” for Muslim Americans. “It was this horrific day that was also, for many New Yorkers, the moment at which they were marked an ‘other’,” he told the New York Times last year.
Last week, Mamdani issued an executive order designating 9/11 an annual official “Day of Remembrance and Service” that requires the city administration to designate a moment of silence to mourn those who were killed and affected by the attacks. A second order established a new taskforce to help the city’s emergency preparedness.
Several other high-profile figures, including former New York governor George Pataki, have voiced opposition to Mamdani’s attendance at the ceremony, and an online petition arguing the same has gathered close to 100,000 signatures.
Dignitaries expected to attend Friday’s commemorations include former US presidents Bill Clinton, George W Bush and Barack Obama, and some other former mayors of New York.
The White House has said Donald Trump is not attending but is expected to commemorate the 9/11 attack on the Pentagon at that site close to Washington DC, a decision that also has also drawn criticism.
US vice-president JD Vance is expected to represent the White House in New York.

Russia Warns Norway With Military Targeting After Tomahawks Deployment

Russia Warns Norway With Military Targeting After Tomahawks Deployment
Russia reserves the right to plan the operational deployment of its weapons against Norway after the arrival of US missile systems capable of launching long-range Tomahawk cruise missiles that can reach Moscow, according to The Moscow Times on September 7.
The response follows the conclusion of joint NATO drills, Operation Atlantic City 26, conducted by the United States, the United Kingdom, and Norway from August 26 to September 4. During the maneuvers, the US Navy transported a mobile four-slot missile module, designed to resemble a shipping container, to the Norwegian city of Trondheim.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
Official Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova stated that these weapons could be deployed for NATO aggression against Russia "for solving tasks of a strategic nature."
She noted that it "should not come as a surprise" to officials in Washington and Oslo that "the locations where American systems are deployed and controlled, as well as their supporting infrastructure, become targets of special focus for Russia’s strategic deterrence forces, including the planning of the combat use of appropriate strike systems in the event of an armed conflict."
Russian officials stated that they view NATO’s actions "as another step in an endless series of highly destabilizing actions."
According to the ministry spokesperson, Moscow will take into account that positioning such hardware in Norway "allows covering an impressive sector of the European part of Russian territory, including Moscow," including with Tomahawk missiles. Russian officials also asserted that Western nations are using these maneuvers to gain control over maritime navigation in the area.
Military domain sources report that the Northern European NATO exercises took place under the broader Arctic Sentry defensive umbrella in the High North. A primary task of the operations was transferring containerized launchers for Tomahawk and SM-6 missiles to evaluate long-range air transport capabilities between regions.
The exercise also tested command, control, and communication networks needed to coordinate geographically separated long-range missile systems within a single joint targeting network, alongside several other military systems.
Previously, the United States considered transferring long-range Tomahawk missiles to Ukraine to significantly expand its deep-strike capabilities against Russian military infrastructure. With a range between 1,600 and 2,500 kilometers and a 450-kilogram warhead, these precision-guided missiles offered a substantial upgrade over existing Ukrainian drone and missile arsenals.
Ukrainian defense officials sought these systems to target deep-rear Russian military airfields, large ammunition depots, defense production facilities, and air defense networks. Despite the missile's origins dating back to the 1970s, modernized variants remained highly competitive against other Western and Russian long-range systems due to their extended range, low-altitude flight profiles, and inflight target redirection capabilities.

Ukrainian AI targeting module placed third among 60-plus entries in NATO contest
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:20:48 UTC
05:20:48 KST

A Ukrainian company has placed third in a NATO contest to find ways of keeping an enemy's airfields shut down over time. Its artificial-intelligence targeting module finished among the top three of more than 60 entries in the Persistent Airfield Denial Innovation Challenge, Ukraine's Defense Ministry said.
The challenge was run jointly by NATO Allied Command Transformation and the NATO-Ukraine Joint Analysis, Training and Education Center, the first jointly staffed NATO-Ukraine body. The result shows NATO is building a direct channel for Ukraine's combat-tested technology into its own capability development.
On the NATO side, the finalists' proposals were evaluated by representatives of the Alliance's Commands, as well as the NATO Defense Innovation Accelerator DIANA.
An AI module lands third place
Organizers received more than 60 applications and brought nine finalists to Warsaw. The Ukrainian team took third place with a module designed to enhance the autonomy and accuracy of strike systems. The Ukrainian Defense Ministry did not name the developer.
A Czech firm, LPP Holding, won with a long-range system designed to work with minimal outside control, and a Polish team came second with a plan for the pre-planned destruction of key airfield infrastructure.
JATEC feeds Ukraine's lessons to NATO
Ukrainian experts helped define the problem and judge the entries, including officers from the Air Force Command, the Unmanned Systems Forces, and the National Guard's Omega unit.
The challenge, which carried up to €250,000 in prize funding, was the second of the two bodies to run together, after a 2025 round that fast-tracked European firms to counter Russian glide bombs.
In July 2026, Russian aviation used approximately 8,000 guided aerial bombs against Ukrainian cities.
The winning solutions now move to testing and combat validation, which the Defense Ministry said will show how well they work and whether they can scale.

Volkswagen plant to be converted for Israeli defence group
Crisis-wracked German auto giant Volkswagen said Monday that one of its plants would be sold off and converted to make defence equipment after car production ends there.
It is part of a sweeping overhaul at Europe's top carmaker, which is already pushing through the biggest job-cutting drive in global auto industry history as it battles Chinese competition, US tariffs and patchy electric car sales.
The announcement is also the latest tie-up between Germany's ailing auto industry and the defence sector, which is booming as countries build up their militaries to face an increasingly dangerous world.
VW's Osnabrueck plant, in northwest Germany, is to be sold to Tel Aviv-based investors Aurelius Capital and the German state of Lower Saxony, a major VW shareholder, with an initial air defence project planned for the Israeli firm Rafael Advanced Defence Systems.
They did not disclose the sale price.
The deal comes as Israel is facing scathing criticism for the war on Gaza, determined by rights groups to be a genocide. The onslaught has killed over 73,000 Palestinians and flattened entire neighbourhoods in the enclave.
"With today's agreement, we are taking an important step towards opening up a new industrial future for the site," Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume said.
"Volkswagen stands by its responsibility for Osnabrueck," he said.
The company is seeking to slash production capacities as it struggles with weak demand, and had already decided in 2024 to end vehicle production at the factory by 2027.
The deal will guarantee that at least 1,200 out of 1,800 jobs are preserved at the factory, VW's works council said.
The project with Rafael will focus on the potential manufacture of systems and components for air defence systems for Germany and Europe, the carmaker said, without giving further details.
"We are building a long-term industrial relationship with our German partners, with the aim that the technology will be fully produced in Germany, in order to protect Germany and Europe," said Yoav Tourgeman, Rafael's president and CEO.
The Osnabrueck site, which dates back 125 years, currently produces the Volkswagen T-Roc Cabriolet as well as the Cayman and Boxster for its sister brand Porsche.
'Opportunities for the site'
The long-term future of four other German factories of the VW group remains uncertain as it cuts costs.
Management and unions last week agreed to look at "alternative uses" for those sites as they signed off on a further 50,000 job cuts, bringing total losses across the group in the coming years to 100,000.
So far, the 10-brand auto giant, whose marques range from Audi to Seat, has managed to avoid any major factory closures in its home country throughout its 89-year history.
Greeting the deal, VW supervisory board member and IG Metall union leader Christiane Benner said the company was not off the hook for the hundreds of jobs not covered by the deal.
"Today's move opens up opportunities for the site, but does not relieve Volkswagen of its responsibility to create solid prospects for the remaining employees as well," she said.
The sale of the plant to Lower Saxony and Aurelius Capital helps VW avoid the potentially thorny issue of dealing directly with an Israeli defence firm, in this case one that makes the Iron Dome air defence system.
Qatar's sovereign wealth fund is Volkswagen's third-largest shareholder, holding about 10 percent of equity, and had reportedly been unhappy at the speculation that VW might directly make parts for Rafael.
Qatar does not recognise the state of Israel.
The announcement is the latest tie-up between the automobile and defence sectors. Mercedes-Benz said in June that it had a deal with drone maker Tytan Technologies to adapt some of its vans for mobile drone defence.
Mercedes has also reportedly held talks with French-German tank and weapons maker KNDS about potentially building armoured personnel carriers at a Mercedes plant.

BREAKING: Ukraine's prosecutor general resigns amid major corruption scandal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:15:55 UTC
05:15:55 KST

Editor's note: This story is being updated.
Ukrainian Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko said on Sept. 7 that he had submitted his resignation to President Volodymyr Zelensky and parliament.
"This is a political decision. And I made it consciously," Kravchenko announced. "I do not want the position of prosecutor general to be used as an instrument of political confrontation," he added.
Kravchenko said his position regarding the allegations against him remains unchanged, maintaining that he was not involved in the alleged scheme.
In announcing his resignation, Kravchenko also thanked prosecutors working across the country.
"I thank my colleagues who honestly perform their work. Those who represent the prosecution in court, work with victims, document Russian crimes, and defend the interests of the state," Kravchenko said.
The announcement marks a reversal from earlier on Sept. 7, when Kravchenko said he had no plans to resign amid an investigation into an alleged protection racket involving scam call centers and senior officials in the Prosecutor General's Office.
The National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAPO) announced on Sept. 5 that they had uncovered an alleged criminal organization led by a senior official in the Prosecutor General's Office that protected fraudulent call centers and laundered millions of hryvnias.
According to investigators, the group was created in mid-2025 and included serving prosecutors and associates outside the Prosecutor General's Office. The group allegedly received systematic bribes in exchange for allowing fraudulent call centers targeting Ukrainians and foreigners to operate without interference.
Investigators allege that proceeds from the scheme were laundered through property purchases, assets registered to third parties, and bank accounts belonging to associates. Five alleged members of the organization have so far been identified.
NABU detained Serhii Kropyva, a deputy head of the Prosecutor General's Office's international cooperation department, in connection with the case. Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court on Sept. 7 remanded Kropyva in custody until Nov. 2 and set bail at Hr 120 million ($2.7 million).
Kropyva is suspected of laundering assets worth more than Hr 89 million ($2 million) and has been suspended from his duties. Another suspect, Yelyzaveta Ivakhnenko, was also detained and had bail set at Hr 20 million ($450,000).
Recordings released by NABU also refer to a person identified as the "boss" who allegedly protected the group and whose patronymic is Andriiovych and who previously headed the State Tax Service — details that correspond to Kravchenko. NABU has not publicly identified Kravchenko as a suspect in the case.
At a Sept. 6 court hearing, a SAPO prosecutor also mentioned the close relationship between Kropyva and Kravchenko. Case materials allege Kropyva arranged repair work at a house in Kozyn, an elite residential area south of Kyiv where Kravchenko lives; Kravchenko later said his family rents the property.
Kravchenko, whose office was searched as part of the investigation, denied any involvement on Sept. 6, saying he had never instructed anyone to facilitate the operation of illegal call centers or used his position to protect them.

Progress MS-33 ends its 6-month mission — Roscosmos
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:10:35 UTC
05:10:35 KST

MOSCOW, September 7. /TASS/. The Progress MS-33 cargo spacecraft has completed its mission, with its non-combustible structural components splashing down into the Pacific Ocean away from inhabited areas, Russia’s state space corporation Roscosmos said.
"The Progress MS-33, which had been operating as part of the Russian segment of the International Space Station since March, was de-orbited, entered the dense layers of the atmosphere, and disintegrated. The unburned structural components of the spacecraft fell into a non-navigable area of the Pacific Ocean," it said.
The Progress MS-33 undocked from the Poisk module of the Russian segment of the International Space Station ahead of the arrival of a new cargo spacecraft at 6:18 p.m. Moscow time (3:18 p.m. GMT). The spacecraft was launched from the Baikonur spaceport on April 26 and docked to the ISS two days later. It delivered around 2.5 metric tons of cargoes, including 1,211 kilograms of dry cargo for the ISS-74 crew and station systems, equipment for the Sun-Terahertz experiment, 828 kilograms of propellant to refuel the station, 420 liters of drinking water, and 50 kilograms oxygen to replenish the station’s atmosphere.

“The High Court’s directive to allow visits to Nukhba terrorists for the first time since October 7 constitutes a direct blow to the State of Israel’s security deterrence," Ben-Gvir said.
He also linked a decline in terrorist attacks to reforms in prison conditions.
“The security reality is clear: There has been a decline of approximately 75% in terrorist attacks, according to the Shin Bet, due in part to the reform of conditions for terrorists in prison," he said.
Ben-Gvir also accused the High Court of serving the interests of Israel’s enemies, saying, “Unfortunately, the High Court consistently serves as an address for appeals by the enemy, and as Justice Amit told petitioners in the case concerning the entry of goods into Gaza, ‘This court places itself at your disposal.'”
Prison conditions, death penalty central to Ben-Gvir agenda
As national security minister, Ben-Gvir has made tightening prison conditions for October 7 terrorists and advancing the death penalty for terrorists key priorities of his term.
When the death penalty for terrorists law first passed in April, Ben-Gvir told The Jerusalem Post that the measure would help prevent another attack like the October 7 massacre, defending it amid international condemnation and saying it would align Israel with US capital punishment policies.
Ben-Gvir has continued to present harsher prison conditions and capital punishment as central elements of his approach to deterring terrorism. Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars in US products took effect Tuesday, as a trade war between the North American neighbours heats up.
The announced duties of 15 per cent, 25 per cent and 50 per cent apply to C$27.6 billion (US$20 billion) in imports from the United States, covering steel and aluminium products as well as dairy goods like cheese. But Canada removed some seafood products from the initial list.
Ottawa’s pushback comes weeks after US President Donald Trump imposed 50 per cent tariffs on a similar value of Canadian products, over what Washington deemed as “discriminatory treatment” against US alcohol, automobile and dairy industries.
The US tariffs hit items like hockey sticks and cement, impacting about 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the United States.
On Monday, Trump threatened to block sales of Canada’s Bombardier Aviation in the United States, unless the Quebec-based plane maker moves manufacturing to the US.
“No more selling Bombardier in the United States!” Trump posted in all caps on his Truth Social platform, though he did not specify how he would achieve a sales halt.

Iran will travel to Japan with a large delegation featuring a combination of experienced champions, established medal contenders and promising young athletes, all aiming to make a strong impact on the Asian sporting stage, accoridng to Tehran Times.
Iran’s final delegation consists of 522 members, including 312 athletes.
The size of the team has generated considerable discussion in recent months. While Iranian officials initially emphasized a “quality-based” approach focused on athletes with genuine medal prospects, the delegation was gradually expanded following the addition of new quotas.
At one phase, 26 additional quotas were added to the initial lineup, raising questions over whether quantity had ultimately taken precedence over quality.
 
 However, a large delegation does not necessarily mean a lack of quality. Iran remains a serious medal contender in several major disciplines, with wrestling, taekwondo, weightlifting and shooting expected to form the backbone of its medal campaign.
Shooting is among Iran’s strongest medal hopes, with 14 Iranian shooters set to compete in Japan.
Weightlifting will also attract significant attention. The Iranian lineup includes established names such as Mostafa Javadi, Ali Aalipour and Ali Davoudi, alongside two female lifters. Yet the competition will be fierce, with Asia’s traditional weightlifting powers leaving little room for error.
Athletics is another discipline carrying high expectations. A target of 10 medals has been discussed, although achieving that figure will be challenging given the gap between some Iranian athletes and the continent’s leading performances.
In canoeing, nine Iranian athletes will compete, with hopes of ending a 16-year wait for an Asian Games gold medal.
In team sports, Iran’s volleyball team remain one of the continent’s leading contenders. Basketball, football and several other teams, however, face tougher challenges. Iran’s U23 football team, in particular, have been drawn alongside China, North Korea and the United Arab Emirates, while limited preparation and a lack of sufficient friendly matches remain concerns.
Beyond the established medal hopefuls, Nagoya 2026 could also provide a valuable platform for Iran’s younger generation. For some, this may be their first major international experience, potentially marking the beginning of a journey toward future success.
With a blend of proven champions and emerging talent, Iran head to Japan with genuine hopes of producing a strong medal haul. From wrestling and taekwondo to shooting, weightlifting, volleyball, athletics and canoeing, the expectation is clear: Iran want to make their presence felt across Asia.
The 20th Asian Games will be held from Sept. 19 to Oct. 4, 2026, in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. As the continent’s best athletes gather for two weeks of competition, millions of Iranians will be watching their national delegation with hope and pride, dreaming of gold, silver and bronze medals and the sight of the Iranian flag rising above the podium in Nagoya.

Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: Lancet
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:04:18 UTC
05:04:18 KST

NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According to a study published in The Lancet Public Health Monday, India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after China, with 444 million Indians affected.While India's age-standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades, the absolute number of people exposed rose from 375 million in 1990 to 444 million in 2023, an increase of 18.4%. The health toll also rose sharply, with deaths attributable to second-hand smoke climbing from 217,700 to 325,600 during the same period.Fatalities among women rose from 113,400 to 156,900, while deaths among men from 104,300 to 168,700 over the same period. Second-hand smoke also accounted for 9.28 million disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in India in 2023, representing healthy years lost to premature death, illness or disability.Dr G C Khilnani, chairperson of pulmonary, critical care at PSRI Hospital, said, "Second-hand smoke contributes not only to illness and disability but also to premature deaths and loss of healthy years. Kids and women are particularly vulnerable, with children's developing lungs making them more susceptible to respiratory issues.
Smoking should be done outdoors, and greater public awareness is needed."The study links second-hand smoke to ischaemic heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, asthma and lower respiratory infections. Among children, lower respiratory infections were the leading contributor to the disease burden.Globally, 2.71 billion people were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to 1.66 million deaths and 44.8 million DALYs. China, India and Indonesia accounted for nearly half of world's exposed population, with China recording 664 million exposed people.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

Nearly 800 children killed, 360,000 displaced by Israeli attacks on Lebanon
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:02:59 UTC
05:02:59 KST

Stephanie Rady and Rania Abushamala
07 September 2026•Update: 07 September 2026
Nearly 800 children have been killed and around 360,000 displaced during nearly three years of Israeli attacks on Lebanon, drawing condemnation from Lebanese officials and groups defending children’s rights.
Israeli attacks continued to claim the lives of children in the past 24 hours, with two children killed and four others injured in an airstrike on a house in the town of Kfar Rumman in the southern Nabatieh district.
Three other children were injured in Israeli strikes targeting the town of Arabsalim and the city of Nabatieh.
The attacks came despite a framework agreement signed under US sponsorship on June 26, which provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory in exchange for the deployment of the Lebanese army.
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun said Sunday that the attacks constitute “a dangerous escalation that goes beyond the repeated violations of the cessation-of-hostilities agreement and the framework agreement.”
Aoun held Israel fully responsible for the continuing escalation and called on the US and the international community to act urgently to halt the violations and hold those responsible accountable.
According to the latest available detailed figures from the Lebanese Health Ministry, 259 children were among 4,362 people killed in Israeli attacks since March 2.
Another 1,050 children were among 12,378 people injured during the same period.
 
Nearly 800 children killed
Lebanese lawmaker Inaya Ezzeddine, who chairs the Lebanese parliament’s Women and Children Committee, said Saturday that “nearly 800 children were killed during the two Israeli wars in 2024 and 2026.”
“A large number of children suffered severe injuries and underwent multiple surgeries, while some lost limbs or eyes,” said Ezzeddine, who also serves as Lebanon’s national coordinator for food systems transformation.
“This means they will need years of treatment and medical care, alongside specialized psychological, emotional, and social support,” she added.
Ezzeddine said around 360,000 children were displaced during the Israeli wars, out of approximately 1.2 million people forced from their homes.
Many children were displaced more than once after areas where they had sought shelter were also attacked, she said.
“Some children were targeted alongside their families on displacement routes or while being forcibly driven from their homes,” the lawmaker added.
Ezzeddine warned that the consequences for children are not limited to physical injuries but also include “invisible wounds” that could have a longer-lasting impact on their lives.
Hundreds of thousands of children require long-term plans for psychological treatment and emotional and social support to help them cope with loss, chronic fear, and a persistent lack of safety, she said.
 
UNICEF warning
UNICEF has repeatedly warned about the impact of the Israeli attacks on Lebanese children and called for an end to the violence.
In May, the UN agency said children in Lebanon continue to pay “the highest price” as a result of persistent violence, displacement, and psychological trauma, despite a ceasefire announced on April 17.
It called on all parties to protect children, comply with international humanitarian law, and take all necessary measures to ensure the ceasefire remained in effect.
Israel has waged attacks on Lebanon since March 2, killing 4,362 people and injuring 12,378 others, while forcing more than 1 million people from their homes, according to Lebanese authorities.
Israel continues to occupy areas in southern Lebanon, some held for decades and others seized during the 2023–2024 war. During the current offensive, its forces have advanced more than 10 kilometers (6.2 miles) into Lebanese territory.

====================================================================================================

Researchers find AI spontaneously develops a sense of facial beauty without training
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
20:00:27 UTC
05:00:27 KST

Artificial intelligence models can spontaneously develop an ability to recognize human facial beauty without any prior training or exposure to human preferences. A recent study published in Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts suggests that this aesthetic sense emerges naturally from the way computer networks process basic visual information. The research hints that human aesthetic preferences might also have an innate origin rooted in our basic sensory wiring.
For centuries, philosophers and scientists have debated whether humans are born with an innate sense of beauty or if aesthetic preferences are learned through cultural exposure. In human infants and nonhuman primates, researchers have observed a natural preference for faces that adults deem attractive. It remains difficult to determine whether this preference is hardwired into the brain before birth or acquired rapidly through early visual experiences.
Deep neural networks, a type of artificial intelligence designed to mimic the human brain’s visual processing pathways, offer a way to test this question. In an untrained state, these networks contain randomized connections and have no prior visual experience or knowledge of human preferences. If an untrained network can detect beauty, it suggests the ability is a byproduct of basic structural encoding rather than a learned behavior.
Researchers Tianxin Shu and Delong Zhang from South China Normal University, along with their colleagues, designed an experiment to explore this phenomenon. They aimed to see if artificial neural units would naturally respond to varying degrees of facial beauty. The research team focused on understanding how simple sensory properties might inherently shape aesthetic perception.
The researchers first generated a dataset of human faces using a specialized artificial intelligence program capable of producing highly realistic images. They manipulated the underlying code of these artificial faces to create different levels of beauty. A small group of human volunteers assessed the images to ensure they still looked like natural human faces.
This process yielded more than 10,000 facial images with distinctly graded aesthetic values. The researchers fed these images into an untrained version of a deep neural network called AlexNet. This network consists of multiple layers of artificial neurons that process visual information, starting with simple edges and moving to whole objects.
Because the network was untrained, its internal weights, which are the mathematical rules determining how neurons interact, were completely random. The researchers analyzed the responses of artificial neurons in the network’s final visual processing layer. They discovered that specific neural units spontaneously began responding selectively to different levels of facial beauty.
These “beauty-selective units” appeared consistently, regardless of the face’s orientation or the specific random initialization of the network. To understand how the network processed this information, the researchers altered the facial images. They applied random scrambling, which disrupted the overall shape of the face but kept local details intact.
They also utilized a different type of scrambling that preserved the general spatial arrangement but obscured fine details. Additionally, they tested images reduced entirely to their simple outlines. The team found that both the specific facial features and the spatial arrangement of those features were necessary for the network to evaluate beauty.
In psychological research, this is known as dual-code theory. This theory suggests that humans rely on both the detailed traits of a face and its broader geometric layout to recognize it. The neural network processed this visual information hierarchically, much like the human visual system.
The network’s earlier layers handled simple geometric features and local details. The later layers then integrated this fragmented data into a complete representation of facial beauty. The research team then tested whether these beauty-selective units could actively compare faces.
They trained a simple sorting algorithm to use the responses from these specific units to judge which of two faces was more attractive. The beauty-selective units successfully differentiated between varying levels of beauty. They performed better than units that simply processed raw image pixels.
The accuracy of these units increased as the difference in beauty between the two faces grew larger. Next, the scientists investigated how the final layer of the network arrived at its beauty preferences. They tracked the activity of units in the earlier layers of the network.
They identified specific neurons that responded to beauty on a sliding scale. The activity of these units steadily increased or steadily decreased as the faces became more attractive. The researchers mapped how these earlier units connected to the final beauty-selective units.
They found that the network constructed its sense of beauty by combining the inputs from these earlier, simpler neurons. Units that preferred highly attractive faces received stronger signals from neurons that increased their activity in response to beauty. Finally, to ensure their results were not unique to one specific network or dataset, the researchers repeated their experiments.
They used a different neural network architecture, known as VGG-16, and again found that beauty-selective units emerged spontaneously. They also tested the network using a database of 200 real human faces spanning different racial backgrounds. The beauty-selective units successfully evaluated the attractiveness of these natural faces.
This outcome proved their ability generalized beyond artificial images. While these findings offer an intriguing look at artificial cognition, a network’s sense of beauty is not identical to human aesthetic appreciation. The study focused on a mathematical abstraction of facial structure rather than the subjective emotional experience humans associate with beauty.
A generalized visual preference for symmetrical or average features does not equate to the rich psychological experience of finding someone beautiful. The artificial faces used in the primary experiments were heavily standardized, minimizing variations in lighting, background, and hairstyle. Real-world aesthetic judgments involve highly variable environments and subjective personal preferences that these models cannot capture.
The current algorithm also primarily evaluated a single baseline standard of beauty. Future research could explore how untrained networks respond to other aesthetic categories, such as natural landscapes, architecture, or fine art. Expanding the criteria for beauty could help scientists determine if this inherent perceptual bias applies to all visual structures or just human faces.
The study, “The Spontaneous Emergence of “A Sense of Beauty ” in Untrained Deep Neural Networks,” was authored by Tianxin Shu, Huawei Xu, Xingxing Chen, Yuxuan Cai, Ming Liu, and Delong Zhang.

Supreme Court judge writes 4th letter to CJI against Raj HC judge
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Judge Sandeep Mehta has written another letter to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant alleging that Rajasthan high court judge Sanjeev Prakash Sharma, who was replaced as the Acting Chief Justice of Rajasthan high court, was interfering in an internal judicial enquiry by abusing administrative powers.This is the fourth letter written by Justice Mehta to CJI on the conduct of the Rajasthan HC judge. His earlier three letters on Aug 2, 10 and 17 had accused Justice Sharma, the then Acting Chief Justice of Rajasthan HC, of "maladministration", "malpractices", "nepotism" and "favouritism". The letter triggered protest from a lawyer in HC and saw the Supreme Court collegium recommending Justice Sanjay K Agrawal's name as Chief Justice of Rajasthan high court, which was approved by the central govt.Justice Mehta had pleaded for the transfer of Justice Sharma, who is retiring on Sept 26, and appointment of a regular chief justice. Justice Mehta also complained as to why CJI Surya Kant had not acted on his fervent pleas.In his fourth letter, Justice Mehta said that he has "further information" and "material" regarding arbitrary, dubious and patently "high-handed" acts of Justice Sharma.
Referring to a complaint committee of high court which was constituted to enquire into allegations against a judicial officer accused of displaying indecent pictures of a fellow woman officer on his mobile phone, Justice Mehta said, "Two Resolutions of the committee dated May 21, 2026, and July 9, 2026, clearly record that the Acting Chief Justice (Justice Sharma) has made direct intervention in the enquiry proceedings, hampering the independence of the committee and that such intervention could vitiate the enquiry as a whole and also breached the confidentiality of such sensitive proceedings.
""The committee also observed that the Acting Chief Justice caused records of the committee to be shared with other officers of the registry and judicial officers, thereby breaching the confidentiality of the enquiry instituted against a judicial officer with grave charges," he claimed.

Cuba says no negotiations with US despite ‘genocidal’ blockade

Cuba says no negotiations with US despite ‘genocidal’ blockade
Cuba reports record losses from the US embargo as foreign minister describes months of punishing blackouts.
Cuba says it is not currently negotiating with the United States, as the Trump administration continues its campaign of economic pressure on the island.
Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez said on Monday that Havana and Washington are not negotiating, and that there is no agenda for future talks.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Photos: Cuba marks Fidel Castro’s 100th birthday
- list 2 of 4Seven decades of US regime change efforts: What have they achieved?
- list 3 of 4US pummels Cuban economy with new sanctions on mining, construction
- list 4 of 4US continues to squeeze Cuban economy with new round of sanctions
His comments came during a media conference, as he laid out Cuba’s latest estimate of the damage caused by the decades-old US embargo, imposed since former leader Fidel Castro‘s communist revolution in 1959.
The Cuban government says the US embargo cost its economy $8bn between March 2025 and February 2026, the highest figure yet recorded and seven percent more than in the previous reporting period.
The total does not include some of Washington’s more recent sanctions, including restrictions on the island’s energy supply imposed in January and secondary sanctions imposed in May, said Rodriguez.
In a post on X, Rodríguez called the policy one of “economic asphyxiation” and described the blockade, which Havana has long blamed for shortages and economic hardships, as “genocidal”.
“These are long months of living with only two or three hours of electricity per day or less,” Rodríguez wrote, painting a bleak picture of what the country’s worsening energy crisis looks like for Cubans.
He described food spoiling without refrigeration, parents fanning their babies through the heat, children trying to do their schoolwork in the dark and young people going without internet access.
“All family life [is] damaged,” he said, adding that Cuba is not a threat but the blockade is.
Rodríguez called the situation “collective punishment”, blaming what he described as a US “energy siege”, an “extreme tightening of the blockade” and secondary sanctions.
Tensions between Washington and Havana have intensified under US President Donald Trump, even after officials held talks earlier this year. Those contacts have since stopped.
The diplomatic fight will soon move back to the United Nations.
Rodríguez said the General Assembly will take up its annual resolution calling for an end to the US embargo on October 27 and 28.
He accused Washington of putting “extraordinary pressure and intimidation” on other UN member states ahead of the vote, but said Cuba still expects “overwhelming support” for ending the embargo.

Sahin Demir

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Monday that Damascus has integrated armed factions into the national army as part of broader efforts to ensure that weapons remain exclusively under state control.
Speaking at the Arab League headquarters in Cairo during the 166th regular session of the Arab League Council at the ministerial level, al-Shaibani said the move was aimed at protecting Syria’s recovery and strengthening state sovereignty.
“To protect this recovery, we integrated the armed factions and rebuilt our national army on the basis of restricting arms to the state,” he said, according to Syrian state media.
He emphasized that the state’s monopoly on arms was a sovereign decision aimed at protecting all Syrians, adding that Damascus had restructured its security and defense institutions to safeguard the country’s borders and sovereignty.
Al-Shaibani noted that Syria has undergone major changes under President Ahmed al-Sharaa over the past 20 months, transitioning from crisis management toward active reconstruction. He stated that the country had ended decades of authoritarian rule, “unified the country,” defeated partition projects, and restored northeastern Syria to state control.
He added that Damascus is addressing societal wounds left by the former regime through “justice and reconciliation.”
“We are steadily moving forward in implementing the three-part roadmap that we worked on with brotherly Jordan,” al-Shaibani said, though he did not provide further details on the initiative.
The foreign minister highlighted that the country has restructured its national institutions and established a new parliament, while placing education among the government’s top priorities. He noted that hundreds of thousands of Syrian children and young people have returned from displaced person camps to schools and universities, while authorities work to rebuild damaged educational infrastructure.
Al-Shaibani also expressed hope that Syria would be integrated into Arab developmental funds and programs by 2027.
Turning to regional conflicts, al-Shaibani stated that Damascus has declared its solidarity with Gulf nations and Jordan since the outbreak of what he described as the “American-Israeli-Iranian war.”
“We reject the Iranian attacks on their territories and the use of weapons outside the framework of the state,” he said.
On the issue of Israel, al-Shaibani welcomed the Arab League’s condemnation of Colombia’s decision to recognize Israel’s annexation of the occupied Golan Heights.
“Syria affirms that Arab rights in the occupied Golan are inalienable,” he said, adding that Damascus remains committed to diplomacy and is working to end Israeli attacks, arrests, and incursions into Syrian territory.
The 166th regular session of the Arab League Council at the foreign ministers level is taking place in Cairo, bringing together top diplomats from member states to discuss regional developments and coordinate policy.

Former Formula One chief Ecclestone detained in Portugal over shotgun aboard private jet
Kyiv • UNN
The former head of Formula One brought a shotgun from Switzerland for clay pigeon shooting without the required document. The weapon was handed over to the authorities in Lisbon.
On Monday, former Formula 1 chief Bernie Ecclestone was detained at an airport in Portugal after police discovered that he had brought a shotgun into the country on his private plane without the necessary permits, UNN reports, citing Reuters.
In a telephone conversation with Reuters from Portugal, 95-year-old Ecclestone said he had brought the shotgun from Switzerland to take part in a clay shooting competition, but did not have the necessary document (the so-called "blue book") to import it.
Ecclestone said he had landed with his wife, Fabiana — vice president for sporting affairs at Formula 1's governing body — at Tires Airport, located near the resort town of Cascais outside Lisbon.
"All that happened was that I brought into the country a shotgun that I had used in Switzerland for clay shooting, so that I could shoot in Portugal — where a demonstration event was taking place this weekend," he explained.
Ecclestone, who does not speak Portuguese, said he passed through customs, but police then asked about the shotgun and demanded the documents, which led to "unnecessary nervousness." As a result, his wife, who was born in Brazil, went to Lisbon accompanied by a customs officer to hand the weapon over to the authorities.
"So now we've been through all this, and the shotgun is with the authorities in Lisbon," he said. "I signed the necessary documents, as they required me to do."
Portuguese newspapers were the first to report the incident, citing police sources; it was reported that the shotgun had been discovered by the authorities during a routine inspection.
We would add
Ecclestone — a former racing driver who ran the commercial side of the sport for around 40 years (until he was removed from his post in 2017) — has a home in a nearby resort area.
The case recalled another incident involving the Briton related to an unregistered weapon: in 2022, he was briefly detained in Brazil for attempting to take a small pistol aboard a private plane departing for Switzerland.
At the time, Ecclestone acknowledged that the weapon belonged to him, but said he was unaware it was in his luggage, calling the incident "stupid" and "insignificant".

Israel’s finance minister has declared the Oslo Accords “null and void” and claimed that Areas A and B of the occupied West Bank also belong to Israel, while calling for the dismantling of the Palestinian Authority.
Speaking at a conference on Sunday, Bezalel Smotrich, who also heads the Religious Zionism party, acknowledged that his position differs from that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
“In any case, Oslo is null and void. In any case, Areas A and B are also ours,” he said.
“That is a dispute with the prime minister,” he added.
Smotrich said Netanyahu had, to his knowledge, ordered the evacuation of sites established in Areas A and B, a decision he opposed.
“Netanyahu, to the best of my knowledge, gave an instruction to evacuate places established in Areas A and B. I don’t like that instruction,” he said.

Smotrich also predicted a major Israeli military operation in the occupied West Bank.

The West Bank was divided into Areas A, B and C under the 1995 Oslo II Accord. The Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) Hindu temple in Paris has released a statement apologising for "any pain or inconvenience caused."
Staff at the Eiffel Tower staged a walkout on Monday, forcing the closure of the iconic Parisian landmark after female employees were said to have been moved out of sight during the visit of a Hindu religious group.
The row began after the visit of around 100 people linked to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) Hindu movement, which inaugurated a new temple in France over the weekend.
Diane Davoine, a union representative, told French TV that female workers had been "moved away from their workstations as the delegation passed by" during a visit on Saturday.
Eiffel Tower employees have condemned in a statement what they described as "professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex."
SETE, the company that runs the tower, has acknowledged that the Hindu delegation requested the trip be organised so as to limit "interactions with women," adding that "these conditions should not have been accepted."
In a statement released on Monday evening, the BAPS Hindu temple in Paris said it took the concerns raised "very seriously" and apologised for "any pain or inconvenience caused."
"Due to the size of our delegation, the visit was arranged in conjunction with the Eiffel Tower team at the start of normal opening hours to avoid disrupting or inconveniencing others," it said.
"To the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower," it continued, adding that it believed in the "universal values of mutual respect and service."
In a post on X, Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire said he was "aware of the outcry among the employees of the Eiffel Tower" and that it was "unacceptable" that such conditions were agreed to.
"These are not my values, nor are they the values that the Eiffel Tower should uphold, where everyone must be able to move about and act freely, without distinction between women and men," he wrote, adding that an investigation into the incident would be launched.
Yaël Braun-Pivet, the president of the National Assembly, has also condemned the incident.
"I refuse to accept that women should be told to step aside to meet the demands of foreign visitors," she said. "Welcoming others never means giving up our values. In France, women are fully present in public life. No one tells them to become invisible there."
The Eiffel Tower's website says the landmark is closed on Monday due to "exceptional circumstances."
It advises visitors with tickets to check their emails and apologised for the inconvenience.
