Movie industry backsliding on gender: director
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:46 UTC
01:40:46 KST

When Danish director May el-Toukhy was selected for the top competition at the Venice Film Festival in July, she was the only female filmmaker in a 20-strong field — with a movie “about the invisibility of women.”
She joked about the irony at a press conference on Sunday, while pointing out that progress on gender bias made in the wake of the 2017 #MeToo movement appeared to be reversing.
“After #MeToo, I think all of us were really aware of this gender imbalance,” she told reporters.
Photo: Reuters
“And something has happened over the course of the last couple of years where we’re kind of returning to, you know, what it used to be — and so we have to be better,” she added.
The protagonist of Woman Unknown is a bride-to-be struggling to hide her wartime secret — a relationship with a Nazi during the German occupation of Denmark during World War II.
Women accused of having consorted with the enemy are seen in the film violently stripped, their heads shaved and red swastikas painted on their bare flesh.
The powerful film, which drew enthusiastic applause after a press screening on Sunday, is “about being objectified on one hand and on the other hand being unseen and voiceless,” el-Toukhy said.
The dearth of females in the top Venice competition has sparked nagging questions about the selection process and female representation.
Festival artistic director Alberto Barbera angered many observers in July when he said the initial 20-1 male domination of the top competition was because the submissions from women “were not enough to put them into the competition.”
Since then, the festival has added another film co-directed by a woman, the documentary NAZA about the Israeli killing of civilians in Gaza, which is to premiere on Thursday.
El-Toukhy, a Danish-Egyptian director who has worked on Netflix’s The Queen, said she had encountered gender bias throughout her career and even with her latest film.
“When I pitched the film to people, I could see that they were glazing over because they were, like, ‘Oh, another Second World War film,’ which I feel is unfair because we’ve told so many stories about the male experience during war or post-war, and we haven’t really explored what it meant to be a woman during that time as much,” she said.
After film school, she said she struggled to find financing for her first film.
“I think it took me six or seven years, whereas my male peers, they were much faster than me,” she said.
“My second film was really hard to get done as well,” she added.
She sees the underrepresentation of women at the top of the industry as a “structural problem” — echoing a similar point made by American star Maggie Gyllenhaalm, who is head of the competition jury in Venice this year.
“I do think it’s much harder for women to get their films financed,” Gyllenhaal said in the first week of the festival.
“Also, could it be possible that the things that women, having had a different experience of being alive in the world, want to make movies about are not always deemed high art?” she added.
Award-winning Italian actress Jasmine Trinca told reporters on Sunday: “When I see that there is only one woman in competition, I’m alarmed, I’m angry.”
“I think it’s a question we really need to ask ourselves and confront,” Trinca said.
A study from the USC Annenberg Inclusion Initiative described last year as a “Great Recession” for women directors in the US: Just nine women were attached to the 100 top-grossing films at the box office.
Only three women have won an Oscar for Best Director: Kathryn Bigelow, Chloe Zhao (趙婷) and Jane Campion.

The Taipei District Court has issued an arrest warrant for an aide of independent Legislator May Chin (高金素梅) after he jumped bail on Sunday.
Judicial police had responded late on Sunday after an electronic wrist monitor belonging to Chang Chun-chieh (張俊傑), Chin’s former legislative office director, issued a low-battery alert, the court said in a statement yesterday.
Police responding to the alert were unable to locate Chang, but recovered his wrist monitor, which had been “broken and thrown away,” the court said.
Photo: Lo Pei-de, Taipei Times
After notifying immigration authorities, the court issued an arrest warrant for Chang.
Chin, Chang and 22 others were indicted on June 8 on corruption and fraud-related charges related to the embezzlement of public funds and the importation of unapproved COVID-19 test kits from China.
Chin, who has denied wrongdoing, was accused of obtaining more than NT$7.87 million (US$249,430) in public funds through fraudulent claims for legislative assistants’ salaries, bonuses, overtime pay and childcare subsidies. This included registering several people, including Chin’s siblings, as legislative assistants, but they did not perform any duties, prosecutors alleged.
Chang was accused of conspiring with Chin to fraudulently obtain funds earmarked for assistants’ salaries, as well as using an indigenous cultural association to fraudulently obtain more than NT$9.33 million from government agencies and state-owned enterprises.
Prosecutors said that during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2022, Chin also authorized Chang to enlist others to illegally import 74,400 unapproved rapid test kits from China, circumventing medical device regulations.
Chin said the rapid test kits were intended to help indigenous communities amid a shortage of the devices in Taiwan.
In the indictment, prosecutors recommended a sentence of at least 16 years for Chang and 12-and-a-half years for Chin.
Chang, who had been detained and held incommunicado for nearly four months before his indictment, was released on NT$10 million bail in June.
At the time, Chang’s lawyers sought his release on health grounds, saying he was more than 70 years old and battling lung cancer.
During the first day of his trial on Tuesday last week, Chang denied the corruption charges, but admitted to other offenses, such as document forgery. He said that he was not just a legislative aide in name, but had performed his duties and had no criminal intent.

Admiring Cabinet’s budgetary acrobatics
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:45 UTC
01:40:45 KST

Over the past few days, opposition lawmakers have harshly criticized the Cabinet for “showing contempt for the legislature” by spending all NT$500 million (US$15.85 million) of the Executive Yuan’s budget that had previously been frozen by lawmakers for the 2025 fiscal year.
The story began in December 2024, when the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) and the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) were reviewing the central government’s budget. Angered by then-Cabinet secretary-general Kung Ming-hsin (龔明鑫) leaving that legislative committee meeting without authorization, the lawmakers in January last year responded by voting to freeze NT$500 million in Executive Yuan funding.
However, after combing through the government’s final accounts for last year submitted at the end of last month, the opposition lawmakers were nearly apoplectic. Not only had the NT$500 million not remained under lock and key, but it had been completely spent.
For those familiar with government accounting, the controversy — which opposition lawmakers have denounced as bypassing legislative oversight — is a case of a rather entertaining bureaucratic sleight of hand.
Opposition lawmakers, in their eagerness to flex their authority, had overlooked an important detail. In their proposal, the KMT and TPP’s resolution simply stated that NT$500 million of Executive Yuan funding was to be frozen, but neglected to specify any particular budget item or program.
As the legislature had not specified which funds were off-limits, the Cabinet assigned the frozen NT$500 million to personnel expenses, the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS) said. Civil servants’ salaries, pensions and related remuneration have strong statutory and constitutional protections. The Cabinet said that it was legally obligated to make those payments.
The Executive Yuan played its apparent submission as an offensive move, finding a legal pathway for it to spend the money. In the end, the Cabinet effectively put the entire NT$500 million to use, a maneuver that spared operating expenses and construction and procurement spending from bearing the full weight of the freeze.
While KMT and TPP lawmakers have been protesting angrily, Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) offered only a brief response to media questions on Friday, saying that the DGBAS had already explained the matter in accordance with the law.
With little legal recourse, it seemed that all opposition lawmakers could do is vent to the media that, in the words of KMT Culture and Communications Committee Director Charles Chen (陳以信), the Legislative Yuan “might as well close its doors” in light of the Cabinet’s workaround.
The act of budgetary subterfuge is another demonstration that, even under the political constraints of a minority government, the administration does not necessarily have to sit helplessly. When faced with politically motivated, borderline frenzied budget cuts and freezes; government officials can still respond with technical expertise and legal arguments.
This battle over government accounting not only demonstrates the political resilience of a minority government, but also shows that if legislative oversight is reduced to political score-settling without technical rigor, lawmakers might ultimately find themselves struck by their own boomerang. It has been a battle of political and bureaucratic wits, and is certainly a worthy piece of gossip.
Richard Wu is a trade promotion organization retiree.

01:40:42 KST

A British racing driver thanked a “superhero” rival for pulling him from the flaming wreckage of his car after a horror crash in Shanghai, saying the quick response saved his life.
Loek Hartog on Saturday stopped and leapt out of his own car to rush to the aid of Ollie Millroy during the China GT Championship race at the Shanghai International Circuit, home of the Chinese Formula One Grand Prix. The Dutchman used a fire extinguisher on Millroy’s Ferrari as a blaze raged before yanking open the driver’s door and dragging him to safety.
“I am still alive tonight entirely thanks to one man,” Millroy posted on social media.
“Loek Hartog stopped instantly with no flag marshals or fire crews in sight and risked his own life to get me out of the car,” he added.
The 36-year-old Millroy suffered a huge impact in the multi-car crash during the race, which resulted in his car erupting instantly in flames.
“I don’t remember anything ... but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life,” Millroy wrote. “One day I will tell our three kids this story and Loek will be the biggest superhero in history in their eyes too.”
“I’m lying here tonight with five broken ribs, broken collar bone, broken hand and finger and a bruised lung, but it could have been much worse,” he wrote. “Thank you Loek. I owe you my life for your selfless act today.”
Hartog, 23, played down his heroics in a social media note posted after visiting Millroy in hospital.
“It was terrifying, and there were moments when I didn’t know if I’d ever manage to get Ollie out,” he said. “But it’s not about what I did. I’m sure many people in my position would have reacted exactly the same way.”
“The most important thing is that Ollie is okay. Things could have turned out very differently today, and I’m truly grateful that they didn’t,” he said.
Millroy’s team, AAI Motorsport, said they would “no longer participate in any races organised by China GT” in a statement that criticized safety standards at the circuit.
The team said Millroy’s car “continued to burn for more than a minute” after the crash, and that “no timely and effective firefighting and rescue operations were seen.”
The China GT Championship organizing committee said in a statement on Chinese social media: “We sincerely apologize for this accident and for the subsequent shock and distress it has caused.”
“We will conduct a thorough review and investigation into this accident, and draw up more comprehensive plans to address any shortcomings,” it said.

Germany’s far-right AfD triumphs, aims fire at chancellor
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:42 UTC
01:40:42 KST

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservatives yesterday licked their wounds after a crushing state election defeat in the ex-communist east, as the triumphant far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) launched a withering attack against him.
AfD national coleader Alice Weidel — basking in the almost 44 percent landslide in Saxony-Anhalt — charged that “no chancellor before has been as unpopular as Friedrich Merz, who has become a major burden on Germany’s prosperous development.”
Merz was huddling with his Christian Democrats (CDU), including defeated state premier Sven Schulze, whose party scored 17 percent, an outcome widely blamed on voter anger against the ruling coalition at a time of economic stagnation.
Photo: Bloomberg
The AfD’s lead candidate in the state, 35-year-old Ulrich Siegmund, said that voters had sent “a signal to Berlin” and took pleasure in mocking 70-year-old Merz, calling him “a very good campaigner” for the AfD.
He said that although his party had narrowly missed out on an absolute majority, it was now reaching out to other parties and individual lawmakers in an effort to build a stable ruling coalition.
“It is a very clear government mandate,” Siegmund said.
While the result sparked jubilation among the AfD’s followers, the prospect of the first far-right government taking charge of a German state since World War II has deeply unsettled other parties, migrants and minority groups.
The AfD in Saxony-Anhalt is labeled a “right-wing extremist” group by Germany’s domestic intelligence agency, and some of Siegmund’s staff are former members of a since-banned neo-Nazi organization.
“I’m scared,” said a 28-year-old man who came from Afghanistan in 2015 and who asked not to be named.
“I have two children here,” he said in Magdeburg, Saxony-Anhalt. “What will happen if I have to leave?”
AfD national coleader Tino Chrupalla sought to dispel such fears, saying that “no one needs to be afraid of us.”
He told Deutschlandfunk radio that his party is not against people with a migrant background, “provided they are integrated, speak German ... and contribute to the economy here.”
Weidel struck a more combative tone, attacking the Merz government and predicting that her party would take power in 2029 national elections.
“The people in this country do not want things to continue as they are,” she said, demanding an end to “illegal migration, open borders, skyrocketing rates of crime committed by foreign nationals, and a refusal to carry out deportations.”
Weidel also slammed Germany’s “disastrous energy policy” and “rampant deindustrialization that is breaking Germany’s backbone.”
Pressure has grown on Merz not just from the far-right, but also from within his coalition, which has struggled to reboot a stagnant economy and has argued over social policy, especially pensions.
The visibly dejected CDU state Premier Schulze on Sunday said that his campaign was not always helped by national government policies, saying that “we often faced headwinds, and that wasn’t always easy.”
Daniel Guenther, the CDU premier of Schleswig-Holstein state, labeled the AfD win “a shocking moment for our country.”
“For the first time since the end of World War II, the AfD — a party whose state branch is classified as right-wing extremist — is close to securing an absolute majority,” he said.
The AfD, founded in 2013 as a euroskeptic protest party, soon transformed into an Islamophobic and anti-immigration party, railing against the open-door policy of former CDU chancellor Angela Merkel.
Merz has vowed to return the CDU to its conservative roots and launched a crackdown on irregular immigration while trying to turn the economy around.
Political scientist Oliver Lembcke of Ruhr University Bochum said: “We are witnessing a tectonic shift in the party system.”
Merz took office with the promise of pushing back the AfD, yet the party has grown stronger, despite the CDU’s shift to a more conservative course.
“This confronts Merz with a question of renewed urgency: What strategy can the CDU use to reverse this trend?” Lembcke said.

Renters should be careful of ‘walkthrough’ scams
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:42 UTC
01:40:42 KST

People looking for apartments should always view the property in person and sign a lease before making any payments, the Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB) said, following reports of scammers posting fake rentals.
Demand for rental housing rises as a new academic year starts each year in September, prompting scammers to target inexperienced renters such as students with fake listings on online rental groups, the bureau said.
The listings often advertise rentals below market rates with attractive interiors; scammers claim they are out of town and offer to mail keys through a convenience store delivery service for self-guided viewings, it said.
Photo: CNA
They send fake convenience store delivery links to steal personal information and trick victims into making bank transfers, it added.
One person came across a rental listing on social media for a studio in Taipei’s Daan District (大安), advertised as newly renovated for NT$10,000 a month including a parking space and eligible for a rent subsidy.
She contacted the “landlord” via Line, who said they were out of town but offered to mail the keys through convenience store delivery for a walkthrough.
The scammer sent a fake delivery Web site where the victim entered her delivery information, after which the site said she had “not completed real-name verification” and instructed her to contact online customer service to verify her bank account.
Misled by the fake customer service, the victim transferred NT$30,000 and bought NT$25,000 worth of game credits at a convenience store, sending the redemption codes to the scammers.
She lost NT$55,000 and realized she had been scammed after contacting police to verify the transaction.
Past rental scams often asked prospective tenants to pay a deposit before viewing the property and then cut off contact after receiving the money, the CIB said.
Scammers have added fake delivery Web sites impersonating convenience store services, using the delivery of keys for self-guided walkthroughs to make the transaction appear legitimate, it said.
People should view the property in person, verify the landlord’s identity and only pay after signing a lease, the bureau said.
Convenience store delivery services should never ask people to transfer money or use online banking for real-name verification, it said.
Anyone who encounters such requests should stop immediately and call the 165 anti-fraud hotline or 110 to report the situation, it added.

India’s resilience depends on diversified trade
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:40 UTC
01:40:40 KST

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s participation in the Shanghai Cooperation Council meeting in Kyrgyzstan was about more than regional security; he used the forum to push for deeper trade links between member states. This is only the latest example of India’s proactive pursuit of trade diplomacy. Last year’s free trade agreement with the UK was followed this January by the “mother of all deals,” a wide-ranging agreement with the EU. And high-level trade talks continue with the US, building on a joint statement of intent issued in February.
The backdrop to this big push is fraught. US President Donald Trump’s sweeping and erratic tariffs are only the latest body blow to the international trading system. The WTO’s Appellate Body, which adjudicates trade disputes between member states, has been decapitated since 2019. Countries are increasingly viewing trade and investment through a national security lens. The rules-based multilateral trade order that the Asian Tigers and China relied on to pursue export-led development has effectively collapsed, with no evident successor in sight. As Antonio Gramsci put it at another moment of profound global upheaval, this is “the time of monsters.”
How might a middle power such as India anchor its trade strategy in such a tumultuous period? The nascent field of geoeconomics offers useful guidance.
Consider the concept of “geopolitical distance.” Political scientists at Georgetown University have built a database measuring the gap between countries at any given point in time, based on voting patterns at the UN General Assembly. Research has shown that geopolitical distance is becoming increasingly important in determining patterns of international economic engagement. Bilateral trade, foreign direct investment and cross-border financial claims fall sharply with geopolitical distance.
This trend raises the prospect of a segmented world economy, with export markets shrinking for most countries. While such “geoeconomic fragmentation” is still limited compared to, say, the Cold War era, the trajectory is worrying. A review of several papers suggests that a full decoupling of the global economy into rival blocs could reduce global GDP by up to 7 percent in the long term. The burden would fall disproportionately on emerging and developing economies, which stand to benefit the most from external market access, unrestricted foreign direct investment and technology transfers.
In this landscape, the best strategy for a middle power is likely to be diversification: building a network of trade relationships sufficiently dispersed so that no single bilateral rupture could cause catastrophic harm. The obvious analogy is to modern portfolio theory: a well-diversified investor is not betting on any particular asset but rather seeking insulation against the failure of a subset of assets. The measure is the standard deviation of a country’s trade-weighted geopolitical distance from all trade partners.
By this metric, India is well placed. It ranks among the top quartile of countries for export diversification across the geopolitical spectrum, and near the median for import diversification. Its trade relationships range from the US and Europe to Russia and the Gulf, with many Asian and African economies in between. It has conspicuously refused to be corralled into a single bloc: abstaining from Ukraine-related votes at the UN and deepening the Quad partnership, while playing a foundational role in the BRICS group and negotiating deals with the US and the EU. Such strategic diversification is enormously valuable in a fragmenting world.
Indian policymakers should draw several lessons from these findings. First, to leverage its enviable spread of partners, India must trade much more than it does today. While the country’s trade-to-GDP ratio of about 45 percent is considerable progress from the near-autarky of the pre-liberalization era, it remains well below the levels achieved by successful East and Southeast Asian economies.
The string of free trade agreements is an excellent start, but more could be done to develop regional trade by joining major agreements such as the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership. Closer to home, trade links among the economies of South Asia remain much weaker than those among comparable groups such as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations. To use one example, they could be strengthened by expanding cross-border energy markets: abundant hydropower from neighbors such as Nepal and Bhutan could reduce India’s dependence on fossil-fuel imports.
Next, India should participate in plurilateral deals struck among various subsets of WTO members seeking to deepen trade in a specific area. The economist Jagdish Bhagwati argued that plurilateral agreements impede first-best multilateral progress, but that argument is irrelevant when the WTO has not made any multilateral progress on lowering trade barriers since the Doha Development Round commenced in 2001. Consider the plurilateral agreement on e-commerce being implemented by 66 members, covering 70 percent of global trade. As a large net-exporter of digital services, India should not only sign on, but seek a leading role in the coalition.
Finally, India should zealously safeguard the diversification it has already achieved, which in turn makes it an attractive partner for countries forging a “China Plus One” strategy or, increasingly, seeking to reduce trade dependence on the US. That means being wary about any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-a-vis third countries. Canada has set an example by walking away from trade negotiations with the Trump administration in part because the US sought veto power over its engagement with other countries.
Of course, Canada is overwhelmingly dependent on the US as an export market, so it is unclear whether its principled stand can succeed. For India, well-diversified to begin with, the case is more clear-cut. A country that has spent decades cultivating strategic autonomy should think long and hard before trading it away for preferential market access, however attractive the terms. India must lean into its position as one of the few countries to combine economic scale, democratic legitimacy and geopolitical breadth to boost trade and remain open to all comers.
Shekhar Aiyar is director and chief executive of the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations.

Airline booking service fees climbing skyward again
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:40 UTC
01:40:40 KST

Starlux Airlines yesterday announced that its booking service fee would be raised to US$33, following a fee adjustment announced in April.
The airline in April raised the booking service fee from US$25 to 30.
The latest fee adjustment applies to tickets issued or reissued from Oct. 7, the airline said.
Photo: Tsai Yun-jung, Taipei Times
China Airlines (CAL) and EVA Airways have raised their booking service fees twice this year. During the first quarter, both increased the fee from US$25 to US$28. However, China Airlines announced on June 9 that the fee would be raised to US$30, starting July 9, while EVA announced on June 30 that the fee would increase to US$33, beginning Aug.1
Tigerair Taiwan, the nation’s only low-cost carrier, raised its service fee this month from NT$300 per flight segment to NT$350 during off-peak season, while fees during peak season were increased from NT$400 to NT$450.
Passengers are charged a booking service fee for the use of the global distribution system, which provides reservation services for airlines. The fee is based on a user-pays principle and applies regardless of whether passengers purchase tickets through an airline’s official Web site, a travel agency or other sales channels.
All four airlines collect the booking service fee as part of the ticket price and any changes to the fee do not require prior approval or reporting to the Civil Aeronautics Administration (CAA).
Separately, China Airlines said it would run seven flights on the Nagoya route using Boeing 777 aircraft from Sept. 17 to Oct. 5 to transport athletes traveling to compete in this year’s Asian Games.
Athletes would be served with a specially prepared meal on flights to Nagoya, featuring sesame oil three-cup pork jowl and creamy wild mushroom shrimp with rice, the airline said.

Prosecutors yesterday filed a criminal charge against a lawmaker and cousin of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr over his alleged involvement in a massive corruption scandal involving bogus flood control projects. RUSSIA
11 killed in avalanche
At least 11 people were killed and six injured after an avalanche struck a group of climbers in the Kabardino-Balkaria region in the North Caucasus, local emergency services said. The avalanche swept down Mount Mizhirgi, one of the highest peaks in the North Caucasus, at about 5pm on Sunday, hitting a group of 33 climbers. As of 9am yesterday, 10 climbers had made their own way down the mountain, while the fate of six others remained unknown, emergency services said. More than 50 emergency workers were involved in the search-and-rescue operation, but efforts were being hampered by difficult terrain and a high risk of further avalanches, they said.
JAPAN
Chiikawa promo canceled
Japanese conveyor-belt sushi operator Kura Sushi Inc canceled a promotion it was running in collaboration with manga character Chiikawa from Sunday after an employee was found to have stolen prizes from one of its stores. The sushi giant uncovered the misconduct through an internal investigation after a large number of items appeared for resale on an online marketplace. The promotional items included capsule toys, cups and pouches featuring the hamster-like character, whose popularity has surged following a hit movie this summer. Kura ended the month-long campaign early on Sunday and offered a temporary 10 percent discount across its stores as an apology. The company is collecting all remaining items from its stores and is consulting with police as it continues its investigation, a spokesperson for the company said.

Some ‘good deals’ can be fraudulent
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:35 UTC
01:40:35 KST

The Administration for Digital Industries yesterday cautioned the public to verify online advertisements with commercial brands’ official Web site to avoid fraudulent mooncake sales ahead of the Mid-Autumn Festival.
Some people made online purchases based on a seasonal gift box ad on social media, it said. The ad claimed it was a limited-edition gift box that contained artisanal holiday treats, with refrigerated home delivery and an early-bird discount offered to attract consumers, it said.
The Web site showed product photos, gift box contents, prices, delivery options and an order form after clicking the purchase link to enter its Web site, which looked similar to that of legitimate vendors, it said.
Photo: Taipei Times
People who placed an order did not verify the offer with the brand’s official Web site or social media accounts, nor did they make sure the purchase link and the seller’s information was legitimate while entering their information and paying, it said.
They did not receive any shipment notification, and several days later, the ad Web site stopped working, it said.
No customer service or store information was ever found, the administration said, adding the complainants finally checked the brand’s official Web site and realized there was no promotion.
The ad was set up by scammers mimicking the legitimate brand, it said.
The administration reminded people to remember four anti-fraud tips while shopping online.
First, do not assume it is an official campaign just because an attractive online ad uses fine product photos or well-known brand names, it said.
Consumers should first check a brand’s official Web site or social media accounts and enter its shopping Web site via officially approved sales channels, the administration said, cautioning against clicking on links for unknown sources.
Second, people entering a shopping Web site should verify the link with the brand’s official Web site and make sure it provides comprehensive information on company name, contact information, address, returns and exchanges, and after-sales services, it said.
Third, do not trust products that come with unusually low prices or discounts before checking with the official Website, it said.
Fourth, do not follow instructions on unknown Web sites to transfer money, enter credit card numbers, or share any personal information, it said.
That can prevent data breaches, unauthorized credit card charges or getting scammed, the administration said.

No shortcut to excellence in chips: TSMC executive
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:34 UTC
01:40:34 KST

There are “no shortcuts” to excellence in chipmaking, said Y.P. Chyn (秦永沛), a top executive at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電), as he received one of Taiwan’s most prestigious industrial technology honors yesterday.
Chyn, TSMC’s executive vice president and co-chief operating officer, made the remarks during a ceremony in Hsinchu County’s Jhudong Township (竹東) at which he was inducted as an Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI, 工業技術研究院) laureate.
“For nearly 40 years, I have always believed there are no shortcuts to excellence in semiconductor manufacturing, and technology research and development,” Chyn said.
Photo: Lin Yi-ju, Taipei Times
He said he had worked with TSMC’s operations teams to overcome “countless technical bottlenecks” and turn advanced manufacturing technologies into mass-production capabilities that helped drive global technological innovation.
Chyn recounted his journey, saying that he joined the ITRI’s Electronics Research and Service Organization after graduating from National Cheng Kung University in 1982, and that the four-and-a-half years he spent there “laid the foundation for my semiconductor career.”
He later joined the newly established TSMC in 1987 as one of its early employees.
Looking back on the development of Taiwan’s semiconductor industry, Chyn called it a “Taiwan miracle” and said the government-backed ITRI had played a critical role at a pivotal time.
He said the ITRI’s efforts to cultivate talent and transfer personnel “laid the talent foundation” for TSMC when the chipmaker was established, helping pave the way for the company’s success and Taiwan’s rise as a global semiconductor powerhouse.
Chyn also thanked TSMC founder Morris Chang (張忠謀) for creating the foundry business model, which he described as “a business model that changed the world.”
He also thanked TSMC chairman and CEO C.C. Wei (魏哲家), former chairman Mark Liu (劉德音), his colleagues and his family.
President William Lai (賴清德), who presented Chyn with his laureate certificate, said Chyn had led teams in achieving yield breakthroughs in processes ranging from 28 nanometers to 2 nanometers, helping cement TSMC’s leadership in advanced manufacturing.
Chyn’s contributions have also helped Taiwan “remain at the core of the global supply chain in the era of AI and high-performance computing,” Lai added.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC, 台積電) is accelerating capacity expansion fivefold this year, but it is still unable to keep up with the booming demand for artificial intelligence (AI), TSMC deputy cochief operating officer Cliff Hou (侯永清) said yesterday. This year alone, the company is building 25 chip manufacturing fabs and advanced packaging facilities worldwide, including 13 plants in Taiwan, which is unprecedented, Hou said at a CEO Summit fireside chat at Semicon Taiwan in Taipei. In the past, the company was able to build five or six factories a year, said Hou, who is also chairman of the Taiwan Semiconductor Industry

PRC could exploit defense gaps: Manila
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:31 UTC
01:40:31 KST

China could see recent cuts to US-South Korean military exercises as an opportunity to reassert itself in the Indo-Pacific region, Philippine Secretary of Defense Gilberto Teodoro said yesterday, though he said Washington had assured Manila that its commitments to the Philippines remained unchanged.
Speaking to Reuters on the sidelines of the Seoul Defense Dialogue, Teodoro said there had been no reduction in US-Philippine military activities, and that bilateral and multilateral cooperation involving Manila continued to expand.
US President Donald Trump’s decision last month to scale back military exercises with South Korea has prompted debate among security analysts over the credibility of US deterrence in Asia and whether rivals such as China could perceive a weakening of US resolve.
Photo: Reuters
“It is a possibility, of course. China is very quick to exploit gaps,” Teodoro said when asked whether Beijing could seize on the move.
“If we’re talking about the Indo-Pacific as a whole, then it may signal some opportunity for China to reassert itself,” he said.
However, Manila had received “definite assurances” from Washington and that there was “no indication” that the changes in South Korea would affect commitments under the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty, he said.
Manila has deepened defense cooperation with the US under Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, including expanded joint exercises and greater access for US forces to Philippine military facilities, as tensions with China have intensified in the South China Sea.
Teodoro said Manila was also broadening security ties with other partners. The Philippines recently concluded agreements with Canada and New Zealand, signed a visiting forces agreement with France, and was negotiating a similar pact with Britain, he said.
The defense chief also accused China of relying increasingly on influence operations alongside military and maritime pressure.
“Definitely it takes advantage of democratic space to co-opt people and to use a free media to expand its distortive narratives,” he said.
The Philippines is pursuing stronger espionage and foreign influence legislation to counter such activities, he said.
Asked about Marcos’ recent remarks that progress was being made toward possible joint oil and gas exploration talks with China, Teodoro struck a cautious note, saying it would be “doubtful” that any economic cooperation could be insulated from longstanding sovereignty disputes in the South China Sea.
Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning (毛寧) yesterday said that China “has always been committed to maintaining peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific region, refraining from great-power confrontation, and hopes that relevant countries can also play a positive role in regional peace and stability.”
Teodoro was in Seoul for talks aimed at expanding defense cooperation with South Korea, one of Manila’s largest arms suppliers.
South Korea has supplied the Philippines with FA-50 light combat aircraft, frigates and other military equipment as Manila modernizes its armed forces.
He said the Philippines was interested in deeper industrial cooperation and emerging defense technologies from South Korea, but indicated that a long-discussed submarine acquisition program remained some way off.
“The submarine program is still under review,” he said, citing questions over mission requirements and the substantial infrastructure needed to support such a capability. “I would say it will be still a way off.”
Teodoro said concerns about China’s actions were encouraging closer security cooperation among countries across the region and could ultimately lead to a more interconnected Indo-Pacific security network.
“I believe so because the motivating factor there is China,” he said.

Air force plans more hardened aircraft hangars
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:31 UTC
01:40:31 KST

The air force plans to build 26 more hardened aircraft shelters as the number of F-16Vs stationed along Taiwan’s east coast is expected to reach 120 when the final shipment of 66 jets procured from the US arrives.
The incoming jets would be stationed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County, augmenting the F-16V Block 20s operated by the 5th Tactical Fighter Wing in Hualien County, officials said yesterday.
The air force plans to allocate more than NT$6.88 billion (US$218.1 million) from next year to 2031 to build the shelters in Hualien and Taitung as part of the implementation of a “one aircraft, one shelter” policy.
Photo: Ann Wang, Reuters
Based on the Ministry of National Defense’s budget proposal for next year, 22 of the shelters would be built in Hualien and four in Taitung. The air force plans to build five general aircraft hangars and related facilities at the Hualien base to house transport aircraft.
The air force’s budget plan calls for NT$65.53 million to be allocated next year for project management, surveying, drilling and preliminary design.
Detailed design, tendering and contract awards are scheduled for 2028 and 2029, with construction beginning in 2030, and construction, inspection and project closeout to be completed in 2031.
The air force said in its budget proposal that during defensive operations, frontline fighter aircraft would be dispersed to the Jiashan and Shihzishan facilities in Hualien and Taitung respectively to preserve combat capabilities.
It needed to reassess the number of aircraft as well as the protective capacity and requirements of existing shelters.
The new shelters would be designed to withstand high levels of explosive force, ensuring that sufficient numbers of fighter jets could be preserved to continue carrying out joint suppression, interception and homeland defense missions in the event of a sudden enemy attack or during a contingency, the air force said.
Once the 7th Tactical Fighter Wing in Taitung has received all 66 F-16V Block 70s, eastern Taiwan would have about 110 to 120 F-16Vs, based on public releases, making the region one of the most important concentrations of Taiwan’s fighter aircraft.
In related developments, President William Lai (賴清德) yesterday urged military officers to adapt to rapidly changing global conditions and advances in technology by putting people first, using artificial intelligence as a supporting tool and remaining grounded in the realities of real-world combat.
Lai made the remarks at the opening ceremony for next year’s class of officers undergoing advanced military education at National Defense University’s Shuaijhen Campus in Taoyuan.
He called on them to strengthen the effectiveness of joint operations and asymmetric capabilities and to prepare for the transformation of the armed forces and future defense planning and combat readiness.
Lai recalled the saying, “Even when a country is at peace, forgetting war will bring danger,” to remind military officers that their resolve to defend Taiwan’s sovereignty and safeguard peace across the Taiwan Strait must not waver.
Only by continuously strengthening and investing in national defense can peace be secured through strength, he said.

Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale yesterday adjourned the Pacific nation’s parliament indefinitely after staring down a no-confidence vote closely watched by China and US allies.
The political drama unfolded as US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau arrived in the Solomons on Sunday, pledging the return of the Peace Corps to the island nation where US Pacific forces fought a pivotal battle in World War II.
Wale is reviewing a security pact struck with China in 2022 as he steers his nation closer to the US and Australia, and was forced to abruptly leave a Pacific islands leaders’ summit last week to fight the no-confidence motion.
Photo: AFP
Diplomats at the Pacific Islands Forum said that the survival of Wale’s government, three months after he embarked on a course to cut reliance on China, would have security consequences for the region.
Several Pacific leaders avoided the summit after China bristled at Taiwan’s presence.
Elected in May, Wale’s government is negotiating a new treaty with Australia, struck a deal to allow US Coast Guard patrols and is in talks for US investment in a port development previously eyed by China.
The motion against him was withdrawn on Sunday by Manasseh Maelanga, its instigator who was sacked as home affairs minister as more lawmakers crossed over to Wale’s coalition. Parliament yesterday adjourned indefinitely, preventing another challenge.
“We hope to come back before Christmas to pass the budget,” Wale told parliament.
“The pace of change is fast,” he added.
The pause will allow time to consider major policy changes, including mining reform and the introduction of free education, he said.
“I imagine that the Australian government will be very relieved,” former Australian high commissioner to the Solomons James Batley said.
“The general public reaction to the idea of a motion of no-confidence would have been very hostile so soon after Wale’s election,” he said.
Australia has criticized the presence of Chinese police in the Solomons, approved by former prime minister Manasseh Sogavare, and is working with Wale’s government to train more Pacific police.

Embrace structured immigration
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:27 UTC
01:40:27 KST

There is no shortage of discussion surrounding Taiwan’s demographic crisis. The government has rightfully, and fairly, attempted to reverse the trend by offering financial incentives to young people to have children. Yet, Taiwan must confront an uncomfortable truth: Cash handouts are not enough. Taiwanese society must accept that managed, large-scale immigration is no longer just an option — it is a necessity. The demographic shift is so deep that even in the unthinkable scenario that every Taiwanese woman of childbearing age begins having three children by next year, it would not be enough.
If Taiwan is to open its doors, the nation must look closely at the historical mistakes made in Europe. Taiwan’s approach must be free of ideology and be deeply respectful, but also unapologetically interest-driven. Immigration only succeeds when host country’s offer potential migrants a genuine stake in their future. Those Taiwan wants to attract need clear, long-term horizons, whether they choose to stay permanently or eventually return home.
Taiwan must abandon the illusion that it can simply bring in foreign workers for a few years to clean the backsides of its aging population and then expect them to vanish.
When Germany adopted its Gastarbeiter (“guest worker”) policy in the 1970s, it assumed the laborers would eventually leave. Instead, the lack of long-term perspectives and systemic discrimination bred poor integration. The result was the emergence of isolated parallel societies in major German cities — a mistake that continues to exact a heavy societal cost. Exclusion breeds rejection.
To avoid this fate, Taiwan’s legal framework requires a massive overhaul, not just minor, superficial adjustments.
First, the path to permanent residency must be clear and standardized. Anyone who has lived and worked legally in Taiwan for five years, earning an industry-standard average wage — rather than an arbitrary multiplier of the minimum wage — should automatically qualify for a permanent residence permit. Maximum stay limits must be abolished; the longer a migrant contributes to Taiwan’s economy through their own income, the more secure their legal status should become.
Second, Taiwan must dismantle the extreme dependence of domestic caregivers on their host families, a power dynamic that frequently invites substandard conditions. If a caregiver’s employment is terminated, they should be granted a realistic five-month grace period to find a new position. Many caregivers face threats of immediate deportation for perceived “disobedience.”
Taiwan must also broadly accept dual citizenship and grant all graduating foreign students an adequate grace period to secure employment. Having already benefited from and contributed to the Taiwanese system, it makes zero economic sense to discard these educated resources.
Ultimately, Taiwan’s immigration system should pivot around one fundamental question: Does the migrant contribute to society? To prove this, presenting a clean criminal record and a valid employment contract paying an industry-standard average wage should suffice. Meaningful labor does not require a master’s degree or a doctorate. Private enterprises are far better suited than bureaucrats to decide whether an employee brings economic value.
While integration carries upfront costs, they are rapidly offset by the long-term economic returns. Taiwan should provide free Mandarin language courses to lower-income migrant groups. Mastering the local language shields workers from exploitation and accelerates their adaptation into the community.
Taiwan must also stop romanticizing the idea that it can selectively recruit only “socially desirable” or elite migrant groups.
When immigrants are given a real future, they are far more likely to lay down roots and raise families. A migrant’s legal status should be positively influenced by their children, with the ultimate societal goal of helping blue-collar families transition into white-collar professions over a generation.
That shift would require an open, honest national discourse on social adaptation. The path forward lies in a pragmatic middle ground between demanding total cultural assimilation and abandoning Taiwanese identity.
Taiwan need a majority culture that fosters inclusion. To achieve this, major corporate leaders must use their leverage to pressure political parties and candidates who resort to xenophobic rhetoric for cheap electoral gains. Hostile, border-line fascist campaigns — such as the rhetoric targeting Indian migrants — must face harsh financial consequences. Pulling corporate campaign donations would quickly quiet down the political opportunists.
Taiwanese do not need to fear “European conditions” if Taiwan implements a well-managed, steadily growing immigration strategy. Coexistence and mutual economic benefits are already a quiet reality in many sectors of society. Anyone harboring irrational anxieties is ignoring that Taiwan’s future prosperity depends entirely on its ability to integrate new communities.
The facts of Taiwan’s demographic decline are locked in. It is time for the nation to grow up, change its laws and build an immigration system based on mutual respect and mutual interest.
Claudius Petzold is a German attorney-at-law.
Taiwan is home to thousands of foreign residents who build careers, families and lives here. However, what happens when one of those residents loses the ability to prove his identity — not because he has broken Taiwan’s laws, but because his own government refuses to renew his passport? That is the situation my husband, Matteo (not his real name), a Nicaraguan national, has found himself in. After about three years of attempts to renew his passport, our future in Taiwan remains uncertain. It all comes back to Taiwan’s giant geopolitical issue: the multitude of countries cutting diplomatic ties with Taiwan
The devastation in Tibet from flooding caused by a glacial collapse in the Himalayas was immediate and profound. Entire communities were left in shock, families were torn apart and countless lives were disrupted. That was followed by deafening silence from the Chinese authorities. No official tally of the missing, no acknowledgment of the dead — only a void filled with rumor, grief and suspicion. Disasters demand transparency. The first responsibility of the state is to inform its citizens of the scale of tragedy. By withholding that information, Beijing reduces Tibetan lives to abstractions, erasing their suffering from public record. The refusal to

FIFA confirms Infantino to run in next year’s vote
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:23 UTC
01:40:23 KST

Gianni Infantino is to stand in the FIFA presidential election in March next year, despite the backlash over his now-abandoned plan to bring private investment into the World Cup, soccer’s global governing body announced on Sunday.
“The FIFA President announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027,” a FIFA spokesperson said. “Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election.”
The 56-year-old Swiss has taken a pummeling since the announcement in late July of his short-lived FIFA Forward Enterprise plan to bring private investment into FIFA events.
Photo: Reuters
However, now for the first time since the plan became public, FIFA has reiterated Infantino’s intention to run for a fourth and final term in next year’s elections.
Should he be re-elected, he would continue to serve as head of world soccer until 2031.
Infantino is in Poland for the FIFA Women’s Under-20 World Cup, but refused to answer queries about his future when questioned by journalists on Saturday.
UEFA has accused Infantino of “criminal mismanagement” over the scheme and was the ringleader of the initial fightback to the announcement, including threatening to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups, if it was not shelved.
However, it has also found solid support from North American body CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).
CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is widely seen as the likeliest challenger to Infantino — UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has ruled himself out. Montagliani, a FIFA vice-president, had long been regarded as a close ally of Infantino, but there were signs, even before he distanced himself over the now-scrapped plan to allow private investment into World Cups, that he viewed FIFA’s purpose somewhat differently to the Swiss.
However, Infantino is not without friends — 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with the Confederation of African Football and South America’s CONMEBOL also supportive.
As the only declared candidate so far for the election, Infantino would need a simple majority of votes from the 211 federations affiliated to FIFA to extend his term of office, which began in 2016 and was renewed in 2023.
Candidate nominations for next year’s election must be submitted by Nov. 18.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:22 UTC

Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz on Sunday posted his most convincing win in his injury return at the US Open, downing Tommy Paul in straight sets to line up a quarter-final clash with Ben Shelton, while all three Taiwanese players played in women’s doubles won.
Hsieh Su-wei and her Latvian partner, Jelena Ostapenko, defeated Spain’s Sara Sorribes and the Czech Republic’s Marie Bouzkova 6-1, 7-6 (7/4).
Wu Fang-hsien and Japan’s Miyu Kato won against Ukrainian sisters Lyudmyla and Nadiia Kichenok 6-2, 4-6, 6-2.
Photo: AP
Another Taiwanese player, Chan Hao-ching and Australian Maya Joint defeated Germany’s Tamara Korpatsch and Argentine Nicole Fossa Huergo 6-0, 6-7 (3/7), 6-4.
Two-time women’s defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also advanced, booking a last-eight date with Wimbledon winner Linda Noskova.
Second-seeded Alcaraz, playing his first tournament since he was sidelined by a right wrist injury in April, looked closer to his brilliant best in a 6-4, 6-3, 6-4 victory over Paul, the 20th-seeded American who posed the Spaniard’s sternest test yet.
“I played my game,” said Alcaraz, who unleashed 33 winners as he moved fluidly around the court, thwarting Paul at every turn in the two-hour 20-minute match.
He is to face red-hot Shelton — a 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 winner over Greece’s Stefanos Tsitsipas — for a place in the semi-finals.
“I tried to play my style,” Alcaraz said. “Tommy is such a talented player. His shots are pretty dangerous and sometimes it’s really difficult to control the ball when it comes to you.”
“I just tried to be ready for a battle and tried to be aggressive all the time,” he said.
Alcaraz grabbed the first break of the contest in the final game of a tight first set.
From there, he was in control. He broke Paul twice in the second set and again early in the third.
He finished it off with a gutsy hold of serve in which he saved a pair of break points, the second with a swinging forehand volley that he followed with a forehand winner to set up the only match point he needed.
“I’m really happy with the performance today,” Alcaraz said.
Shelton, who needed four sets in each of his first three matches, raised his game to dismantle former world No. 3 Tsitsipas in just one hour and 52 minutes.
The American, riding high after a strong August that included a title at the ATP Montreal Masters, blasted a dozen aces and never faced a break point.
“I played a complete match from start to finish,” Shelton said. “I think the level that he’s [Alcaraz] been playing at is really, really impressive. To not play for five months then do what he’s done so far this tournament has been super-human.”
“I think it’s going to be fireworks on Tuesday night,” Shelton said.
Sabalenka kept her bid for a rare US Open three-peat on track with a 6-4, 6-3 victory over the US’ Taylor Townsend.
The Belarusian, whose world No. 1 ranking is on the line in New York, is to face a tough quarter-final against sixth-ranked Czech Noskova, who edged dangerous Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk 7-5, 5-7, 6-4.
Sabalenka needed all her resolve against the multi-faceted Townsend, whose blistering service returns and net prowess flummoxed the Belarusian star in a first set that opened with five breaks of serve.
However, her sustained power and precision proved too much, and after falling behind 3-1 in the second set, she won the last five games to seal the match.
“I was just trying to stay focused on myself and play not only point by point but ball by ball,” Sabalenka said. “I’m happy that I was able to turn around that second set.”
Noskova needed six match points to seal her victory over Kostyuk, failing to convert two in the second set.
“I am more than relieved,” Noskova said. “This match was so tough, emotionally more so than physically.”
The US’ Frances Tiafoe, the 11th seed who has twice reached the semi-finals in Flushing Meadows, booked his quarter-final berth with a 7-6 (7/1), 6-4, 7-6 (8/6) victory over former champion Daniil Medvedev.
“Hell of a match,” Tiafoe said. “I played well when it counted.”
Tiafoe is to face compatriot Alex Michelsen for a place in the semi-finals. Michelsen defeated Argentina’s Tomas Martin Etcheverry 7-6 (8/6), 6-4, 6-4.
Women’s third seed Jessica Pegula also advanced the US cause. Pegula, one of the players with a chance to supplant Sabalenka atop the rankings in New York, reached the last eight with a 6-3, 6-4 victory over Romanian Sorana Cirstea.
She is to play fellow American Emma Navarro, who defeated Anna Kalinskaya 6-4, 6-2.

Kai Havertz equalized in the first half for Arsenal, which have a 100 percent record after three games and moved level at the top of the standings with Manchester City.
Photo: Reuters
“From start-to-finish it, was a joy to watch our team play and compete. The threat we created, huge individual performances as well, the atmosphere inside the stadium was something great to witness,” Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said.

Arsenal faced down the challenge of a Chelsea team that are expected to be among their main rivals for the title this season. It was not only the result that would have sent out a message to the likes of Man City and Liverpool, but the nature of the win.
Chelsea got off to a perfect start when Rogers volleyed low from the edge of the area to beat David Raya in the second minute, but Arsenal produced the response of champions by creating a slew of chances before Havertz fired into the corner in the 25th.
Odegaard’s decisive strike came five minutes into the second half as he finished clinically from inside the box.
“It was a big massive game, a tough opponent, really hard for us against a really good team. It was a big fight, and we got there in the end,” Odegaard said. “We always want to keep fighting and have showed that many times. Conceding early is never ideal, but our reaction was top, [we] could have scored some more goals and got our reward. I think it was a brilliant performance.”
It was the first defeat for new Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, but his team pushed Arsenal all the way, with Raya producing an outstanding save to deny substitute Estevao from equalizing late on.
Pedro Neto also hit the post in the first half.
“It hurts, a defeat has to hurt,” Alonso said. “I learned about the game, about us, what we are doing and starting, the players have this attitude, desire to compete better game-by-game to try to create something we believe in, to have this conviction.”
“So far I’m happy knowing it’s a process, but we want to win games, that’s the ultimate goal,” he said.
Ainsley Maitland-Niles struck in added time to rescue a 2-2 draw for Everton against United.
The deadline day signing came off the bench to make his debut and curled a brilliant long-range shot into the top corner to salvage a point for his new club.

The government has earmarked a record NT$49.9 billion (US$1.58 billion) in subsidies for local MRT construction next year, more than five times the amount budgeted for this year and the highest annual allocation for local MRT projects to date, the Ministry of Transportation and Communications said yesterday.
The ministry hosted a news conference to present statistics after local governments in Taipei, New Taipei City, Taoyuan and Taichung accused the central government of curtailing the budget for the MRT projects in their localities and sought additional funding.
Deputy Minister of Transportation and Communications Wu Sheng-yuan (伍勝園) said yesterday the central government determines its subsidies based on the progress of individual projects, taking into account factors such as construction schedules, tender awards and budget execution.
Photo copied by Wang Jung-hsiang, Taipei Times
The central government has provided more than NT$716.1 billion in subsidies for local MRT projects over the years, with Taipei, New Taipei City and Keelung accounting for NT$488.2 billion, or about 68 percent, Wu said.
For subsidies to be allocated for next year, Wu said the amount was determined following a meeting with local governments officials on May 4 on the progress of their MRT lines. Some are still in the planning stage, while others are already under construction, he said. The average subsidy rate for local MRT projects was about 80 percent last year, Wu said.
Approved subsidy funding for the Taipei-Keelung-Taoyuan region for next year is about 80 percent of its overall budget request, while the figure for southern Taiwan is about 70 percent, Wu said, adding the ministry has made similar fiscal arrangements in the same way in the past few years.
New Taipei City has requested an additional NT$5.4 billion after its MRT subsidies were cut in next year’s budget and has formally asked the ministry to prioritize restoring the cut. Taipei said it is short NT$6 billion in central government funding, while Kaohsiung says it has a NT$13.6 billion shortfall. Wu said there is no indiscriminate spending of public funds for MRT projects. The ministry has established review guidelines for subsidies for MRT construction projects, he said. Local governments submit their funding needs, after which the ministry reviews the proposed projects and assesses whether the funding is warranted, he said, adding that projects with unclear plans would not be approved.
All projects are subject to rigorous scrutiny at every stage, including an initial review by the Railway Bureau, a review by the ministry and an assessment by external committee members.
The ministry said that an amendment to the Act Governing the Allocation of Government Revenues and Expenditures (財政收支劃分法) last year has reduced the central government’s financial resources available for local infrastructure.

EDITORIAL: Trump keeps pressure on Fed
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:18 UTC
01:40:18 KST

US President Donald Trump on Friday threatened to halt trade with countries that have trade surpluses with the US unless the US Federal Reserve cuts interest rates. Trump’s ultimatum came after the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that US employers added 162,000 jobs last month, about triple the number that many economists had expected. In addition, employment data for June and July were revised up, with July rising from a job loss to a gain of 21,000 jobs and June rising to a gain of 31,000 jobs, while the unemployment rate held at 4.1 percent, the data showed.
Trump’s rationale, according to his Truth Social post, was that the strong jobs report means that the US is in a better credit position “than it was just a short time ago.” That should entitle the US to a lower interest rate or even the lowest in the world, he said. However, from the perspectives of mainstream economics and monetary policy, and based on the reality of international trade, the logic behind Trump’s threat to suspend trade with countries running a trade surplus with the US if the Fed does not cut rates is unreasonable and even self-contradictory.
First, Trump appeared to forcibly align the Fed’s monetary policy with US trade, but the central bank’s mandate is to maintain price stability and maximize employment, not to improve the country’s trade deficit. In his attempt to leverage trade sanctions to force the Fed to cut rates, Trump ignored the economic reality that rate cuts would exacerbate inflation when the economy and job market gain steam.
Second, Trump seems to believe that high rates lead to a stronger US dollar, which would weaken the competitiveness of US goods and result in trade deficits. However, if the Fed cuts rates, lower borrowing costs would likely stimulate domestic consumption and investment demand in the US. That could simultaneously prompt the US to import more foreign goods if domestic industries cannot meet the increased demand, widening trade deficits even further, counter to Trump’s intention.
Third, threatening to halt trade with countries with which the US has trade deficits is too radical. As the US is highly dependent on imports in many key sectors, such as consumer electronics, auto parts and semiconductor materials, his threat, if carried out, would lead to severe shortages of goods in the US. The supply constraints would trigger severe price spikes, cripple the US manufacturing sector and plunge the economy into stagflation. In that scenario, the Fed would be even less likely to cut rates, and instead be forced to raise them to curb inflation.
Trump’s remarks appeared to have no impact on US Treasury yields, Wall Street stock indices or the US dollar, indicating that the market generally ignored the US president’s post, viewing it as emotional venting rather than a credible policy threat.
However, Trump’s renewed pressure on the Fed to cut rates further complicates matters for Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, who — at his debut at the annual gathering of global central bankers in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, late last month — reaffirmed the central bank’s 2 percent inflation target as non-negotiable and emphasized that restoring price stability remained the central objective of the Fed’s monetary policy.
At Jackson Hole, Warsh offered a clear analysis and constructive assessment of the US economy, but refrained from giving traditional forward guidance as expected. Still, in his speech, Warsh signaled that under his rein, the Fed would be more disciplined, rules-based and inflation-centric. Even though Trump handpicked Warsh to replace Jerome Powell, Warsh’s hawkish tone in Jackson Hole and his commitment to protecting the Fed’s independence during his US Senate confirmation hearing in April, along with encouraging US economic data, indicate that he would likely prioritize combating inflation rather than responding to Trump’s political pressure.
However, the real test would come this week when the US releases the consumer price index for last month, which is the final major inflation gauge before the Fed policymakers meet next week. If the data show no meaningful changes, or even an uptick in inflation, and yet the Fed still stays put, Warsh would have to present a new rationale. Otherwise, the market would again question the Fed’s credibility and capability, while investors would wonder if Warsh is really an inflation fighter or if he just talks tough while yielding to political compromise ahead of the US midterm elections on Nov. 3.

Cinema under the stars
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:17 UTC
01:40:17 KST

On selected weekends, moviegoers settle into reclining deckchairs on Dream Plaza’s rooftop garden in Taipei’s Xinyi District (信義). Wearing wireless headphones and surrounded by city lights, they watch everything from romantic favorites to independent films and Hollywood hits.
Skyline Film (屋頂電影院 ) has become an established fixture in Taipei’s outdoor entertainment scene. When Joe Chao (趙冠喬) and his collaborators staged their first screening in 2016, however, it was still an experiment inspired by the open-air cinemas he had encountered in London.
IF YOU BUILD IT, THEY WILL COME
Photo: Ben Lee
Back in 2016, this rooftop cinema concept started out as a side project for Chao.
“We wouldn’t call ourselves movie buffs... but we have watched a lot of movies,” Chao said.
The inspiration came when Chao was living in London and attended several open-air cinemas.
“I remember going to a Romeo and Juliet screening in an old, abandoned chapel,” he said. “It was an interesting concept… to watch a movie and see the city from different rooftops over a couple drinks.”
Then in 2016, the first ever rooftop screening became a reality after many months of preparation to secure the location, equipment, screening licenses and other operational hurdles.
The eventual success led Chao to hold regular viewings in 2017.
BEHIND THE SCENES
Movies range from quirky arthouse indies to classics like Casablanca, as well as the latest commercial films.
“Initially, the movie curation process was based primarily on our own personal preference, as it was difficult to know what the audience liked,” Chao said.
Over the years, Chao discovered that romance is the genre that resonates most with audiences, with About Time, La La Land and the Before trilogy among the most popular titles.
But not every pick lands with the audience.
Chao said that he received a lot of negative feedback after a screening of the black comedy Frank.
They’ve also shown blockbuster titles like The Revenant and Dune at one of their Fulong Beach screenings in New Taipei City.
“Watching Dune on the beach with sand right at your feet was a cool experience. The setting created a powerful connection with the film,” Chao said.
THE EXPERIENCE
After checking in, audiences can explore the rooftop garden and check out the views. A concession stand offers snacks and beverages (no outside refreshments allowed).
Each guest receives a pair of noise-cancelling wireless headphones with adjustable volume. One viewer, however, said the headphones did not completely block the noise of a nearby ventilation fan.
The seats are reclined canvas deckchairs, and while they appeal to most, they may be a trade-off for some.
Attendee Lin Hsiao-i (林烋毅) said that they aren’t as supportive as standard theater seating and can be taxing on the back.
For Wang Yu-tzu (王郁慈), however, the setup is just right.
“[Watching] a movie with the sky and cityscapes in the background really makes you feel at ease.”
As the credits roll, a few people hang around for one last look at the night sky and a take few quick snaps before heading for the exits.

Health ministry moots more vaccines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:16 UTC
01:40:16 KST

Deputy Minister of Health and Welfare Lin Ching-yi (林靜儀) yesterday said if a batch of 200,000 doses of enhanced influenza vaccines, which are to be introduced for the first time into the publicly funded vaccination program next month, prove to be effective, the ministry would purchase more next year.
The Federation for the Welfare of Taiwan’s Seniors yesterday held a news conference in Taipei to promote flu vaccination and disease prevention among older people, inviting health officials, physicians and lawmakers.
The federation’s chairperson Fang Li-hsiu (方力脩) said Taiwan has been providing publicly funded flu vaccines to older people for almost 30 years, but with changes in population structure, vaccine development and long-term care services, policies for older people should keep up.
Photo: Taipei Times
He said the federation appreciates the government policy of introducing enhanced flu vaccines in the public-funded vaccination program this year, but the amount purchased this year is very limited, and they hope more can be offered to older people next year.
The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) last month announced that among the more than 7 million doses of publicly funded flu vaccines purchased for the new flu season starting in October, 200,000 doses of enhanced flu vaccines are included, which would be prioritized for long-term care facilities.
At the event, CDC Director-General Philip Lo (羅一鈞) yesterday said Taiwan is the first country in Asia to include enhanced flu vaccines in its national vaccination program.
There are two brands of enhanced flu vaccines this year, a vaccine by TTY Biopharm, which would be available from Oct. 1, and a vaccine by Sanofi that would be available later in the same month, he said, adding that residents and workers of 11 types of long-term care facilities would be eligible for the new vaccines.
Flu activity is climbing early this year, with more than 100,000 medical visits for flu-like illnesses already reported in a week, and flu viruses are expected to spread faster with students returning to school. Infection risk for adults and older adults is likely to increase when it enters an epidemic period.
Huang Li-min (黃立民), a professor of National Taiwan University Hospital, said that older people might have a weaker immune response to the traditional flu vaccines, but the enhanced vaccines can improve the defensive performance by about 20 percent.
Lin said Taiwan’s COVID-19 prevention performance received international praise, but disease prevention measures should be practiced every day, and as Taiwan is a super-aged society, it is important that the senior population get correct information about vaccines and get vaccinated.
She said if many people are willing to get the enhanced flu vaccines and they prove effective, then the ministry would try to acquire up to 600,000 doses for the publicly funded vaccination program next year.

NASA’s newest space telescope launches on a quest to explore the hidden universe  NASA最新太空望遠鏡升空 探索宇宙奧祕
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
16:40:15 UTC
01:40:15 KST

NASA’s new flagship astronomical observatory was launched into space from Florida on Aug. 10 on a mission to probe some of the biggest mysteries in astrophysics and cosmology.
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a roughly US$4 billion project, was carried aloft from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket through blue skies just after sunrise, embarking on a potentially decade-long observation mission.
The telescope, which will park itself beyond the moon, is designed to investigate cosmic enigmas such as dark energy and dark matter, while also testing gravity at vast scales and searching for exoplanets — planets beyond our solar system.
Photo: AP 照片：美聯社
Roman will travel through space toward an orbital location called Lagrange Point 2, situated about 1.6 million km from Earth. Its mission is planned for five years, though the US space agency said the telescope may have enough fuel for five additional years.
Mission scientists will spend the next 90 days commissioning the spacecraft and preparing the observatory for its science operations. It is expected to beam back its first high-resolution images “before the winter holidays,” Roman telescope project manager Jackie Townsend told reporters.
Roman will build on the capabilities of other orbiting observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, and the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990.
Photo: Reuters 照片：路透
“It will be as if Hubble and James Webb kind of peered through a keyhole at the universe, while Nancy Grace Roman will kick the door down,” Nicola Fox, chief of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate, told reporters on Aug. 29.
“Roman has broadly the same sensitivity and sharpness of vision as Hubble, but we survey the sky much faster,” Julie McEnery, Roman’s senior project scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland, told reporters at a briefing in July.
McEnery said one month of Roman observations can survey our entire home galaxy.
“One month of observations to survey our Milky Way galaxy would take about a century with Hubble,” McEnery said.
WIDE ANGLE AND ZOOM LENSES
Webb has provided a new understanding of the early history of the universe, finding among other things that primordial galaxies formed sooner and were bigger than previously known. Webb is capable of looking across vast distances and back into deep time, because of the time it takes light to travel.
Roman instead is able to take panoramic views. NASA likens Roman to a camera’s wide-angle lens and Webb to a zoom lens.
Roman will help in the understanding of two mysterious cosmic components — dark energy and dark matter — by creating the most comprehensive 3D map of the universe to date. Its main survey, to take more than a year to complete, will cover more than two billion galaxies.
The Big Bang event roughly 13.8 billion years ago initiated the universe, which has been expanding ever since. Scientists in 1998 disclosed that this expansion was actually accelerating, with an invisible force called dark energy as the hypothesized reason.
The universe’s contents include ordinary matter — stars, planets, gas, dust and all the familiar stuff on Earth — as well as dark matter and dark energy. Ordinary matter represents perhaps 5 percent of the contents. Dark matter, known through its gravitational influences on galaxies and stars, may represent about 27 percent. Dark energy may represent about 68 percent.
Using Roman to gauge dark matter’s pull and dark energy’s push across the universe will bring scientists closer than ever before to solving both mysteries, according to NASA.
Roman also will conduct one of the most comprehensive searches ever for exoplanets. It is expected to discover thousands of new ones and provide the first statistical census of planetary systems similar to our own.
(Reuters)
美國太空總署（NASA）最新一代旗艦級天文觀測器 8月30日於美國佛羅里達州發射升空，其任務是探索天體物理學及宇宙學最大的一些謎團。
這項耗資約40億美元的「南希．格蕾絲．羅曼太空望遠鏡」（Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope）計畫，由SpaceX的「獵鷹重型」（Falcon Heavy）火箭搭載，在當天日出後不久，從NASA甘迺迪太空中心升空進入藍天，展開這項可能長達10年的觀測任務。
羅曼太空望遠鏡將進入比月球更遠的太空，主要研究暗能量與暗物質等宇宙謎團，同時測試大尺度下的重力作用，並搜尋系外行星，也就是太陽系以外的行星。
羅曼望遠鏡將前往稱為「拉格朗日點2」（Lagrange Point 2）的軌道位置，距離地球約160萬公里。任務原定執行5年，但NASA表示，望遠鏡所攜帶的燃料可能足以再延長5年。
科學家將利用接下來90天進行太空船啟用與測試，並為天文觀測任務做準備。羅曼太空望遠鏡計畫經理傑姬．湯森告訴記者，預計望遠鏡將在「冬季假期前」傳回第一批高解析度影像。
羅曼太空望遠鏡將延續其他太空天文台的能力，例如2021年發射的詹姆斯．韋伯太空望遠鏡（James Webb Telescope），以及1990年發射的哈伯太空望遠鏡（Hubble Space Telescope）。
NASA科學任務理事會主管妮可拉．福克斯8月29日對記者表示：「這就好比，哈伯望遠鏡與韋伯望遠鏡只是透過一個鑰匙孔窺探宇宙，而羅曼望遠鏡則會直接把門踹開」。
位於馬里蘭州的NASA戈達德太空飛行中心（Goddard Space Flight Center）羅曼望遠鏡計畫資深科學家茱莉．麥肯納里7月在簡報會中表示：「羅曼望遠鏡的靈敏度與視覺解析度大致與哈伯望遠鏡相當，但羅曼望遠鏡觀測天空的速度要快得多」。
麥肯納里表示，羅曼望遠鏡只需一個月的觀測，就能掃描我們所處的整個銀河系。
她說：「要完成對銀河系的觀測，哈伯望遠鏡需費時約一個世紀；羅曼望遠鏡只需要一個月」。
廣角與變焦鏡頭
韋伯望遠鏡已讓我們對宇宙早期歷史有新的理解，包括發現原始星系形成的時間，比過去所認為的更早，規模也更大。由於光線傳播需要時間，韋伯望遠鏡能夠觀測極其遙遠的距離，也就等於回望宇宙遙遠的過去。
羅曼望遠鏡則能夠拍攝宇宙的全景影像。NASA將羅曼望遠鏡比喻為相機的廣角鏡頭，而韋伯則像是變焦鏡頭。
羅曼望遠鏡將繪製迄今最完整的宇宙三維地圖，以協助科學家了解兩種神秘的宇宙成分——暗能量與暗物質。這項主要巡天觀測任務預計耗時一年以上，將涵蓋超過20億個星系。
約138億年前發生的大爆炸（Big Bang）開啟了宇宙，而宇宙此後便持續膨脹。科學家在1998年公布的研究指出，宇宙膨脹其實正在加速，而假設中的一種無形力量——暗能量——可能就是造成加速膨脹的原因。
宇宙的組成包括普通物質——恆星、行星、氣體、塵埃，以及地球上所有我們熟悉的物質——還有暗物質與暗能量。普通物質可能只占宇宙總成分約5%。暗物質可透過其對星系與恆星產生的重力作用被觀測到，可能約占27%；暗能量則可能約占68%。
NASA表示，利用羅曼望遠鏡測量暗物質在宇宙中的引力，以及暗能量推動宇宙膨脹的力量，將使科學家比過去更可能解開這兩大謎團。
羅曼望遠鏡也將進行有史以來最全面的系外行星搜尋行動之一。預計將新發現數千顆太陽系以外的行星，尋找類似我們太陽系的行星系統，並建立首次統計普查。
